And one honest run costs 1,150 steps rather than under 300, because the loop is genuinely long. The margin is therefore 3.37 x 10^5, not above 10^8: real, and three orders short of the claim. The clause that held is the one AH3 predicts: the margin is IDENTICAL under an instruction tick and a device tick, because the work factor cancels out of a ratio exactly. Quote the margin as a ratio and it is a statement about the state space alone; quote it in seconds and the work factor is the whole story. Both are true and they answer different questions.

entries.subject: The n+1 arity ladder, and the feedback functions that make a trajectory graph tree-like
entries.claim: the Ladder's history operator replicates past the nine steps it was checked over, with no genesis exception
entries.note: H(prev) = SUM prev + [prev != empty] reproduces Fibonacci with two zeros at the front for all 40 terms checked, against the 9 the Ladder itself verified, and there is no special case at the genesis -- which is the operator's whole claim to being more fundamental than the two-term recurrence. Three of the four competing rules fail exactly where the Ladder says: cur+last first at step 1, sum(prev) wrong at 8 of 9, sum(prev)+1 first at step 0. The fourth disagrees -- my reconstruction of "cur + len(prev)" first fails at step 2 where the Ladder records 6 -- and that is a fact about reading a four-word label, not about its result. The definitions were left as read rather than tuned until they agreed, which would be fitting the instrument to the answer.

entries.subject: The n+1 arity ladder, and the feedback functions that make a trajectory graph tree-like
entries.claim: the arity ladder cubes at every rung, and passes the width ladder at n = 3
entries.note: Exact at every rung: 27, 19,683, 7,625,597,484,987, then a 39-digit number, each the cube of the last because 3^(3^(n+1)) = (3^(3^n))^3. This is a different growth law from the one this project has been using. AD4's width ladder MULTIPLIES by 729 per live word; the arity ladder CUBES. Arity passes width at n = 3 and by n = 4 they are not in the same range -- 39 digits against 15. Adding an input is not a bigger version of adding a word, it is a different operation.

entries.subject: The n+1 arity ladder, and the feedback functions that make a trajectory graph tree-like
entries.claim: the reversible fraction is (2/9)^(3^(n-1)), and it reproduces AB1's swept 1.097% from a formula
entries.argument: A function is reversible in its leading argument exactly when each of its 3^(n-1) columns is a bijection of three values. So the count is 6^(3^(n-1)) and the fraction (2/9)^(3^(n-1)), for every n — a closed form, not a fit.
entries.note: A function is reversible in its leading argument exactly when each of its 3^(n-1) columns is a bijection of three values, so the count is 6^(3^(n-1)) and the fraction (2/9)^(3^(n-1)). AB1 measured 216 of 19,683 by sweeping every table one at a time; the formula gives the same figure to four significant figures without a sweep, and 216 is exactly 6^3. SO AB1 WAS ONE RUNG OF A LADDER NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN. The fraction collapses fast -- 22.22%, 1.097%, then 0.000132% -- which is the arity version of the scarcity M1 found at fixed width.

entries.subject: The n+1 arity ladder, and the feedback functions that make a trajectory graph tree-like
entries.claim: a leading-argument-reversible feedback function makes the shift-register state map a bijection, so no two trajectories ever merge
entries.argument: With state (x1..xn) and next (x2..xn, f(x1..xn)), a leading-argument-reversible f makes the state map injective: two states with the same successor would need the same tail and the same f-value, forcing them equal. Holds for every n.
entries.note: HELD, and it answers what AH2 left open. Taking an n-input function as shift-register feedback -- state (x1..xn), next (x2..xn, f(x1..xn)) -- a leading-argument-reversible f makes the state map a BIJECTION: maximum in-degree exactly 1, zero unreachable states, every one of the 531,441 states with in-degree 1. Nothing merges, so a tabulator's reuse is exactly 1.00 against AH2's 3.20 and hailstone's 10.43, and there is nothing to amortise. The non-reversible comparison is worse than predicted rather than better: tritwise MIN gives a maximum in-degree of 729 and leaves 91.22% of the state space UNREACHABLE, against a predicted quarter. So AB1's 216 tables are not a curiosity. THEY ARE EXACTLY THE FEEDBACK FUNCTIONS THAT MAKE THE FOURTH FACTOR COME OUT RIGHT, and this project measured them four sets before it knew what they were for.

entries.subject: What self-reference buys, and what actually buys the property it is asked for
entries.claim: the ladder step carried in two words is injective, with in-degree exactly 1 everywhere, because every component is ADD
entries.argument: Every component is ADD, which erases nothing, and the inverse is explicit: from (sum+lag, sum+1) recover sum = second - 1 and lag = first - sum. An explicit inverse is a proof of injectivity, not evidence of it.
entries.note: Maximum in-degree 1, zero unreachable, over all 531,441 (sum, lag) states -- AI4's bijection criterion met with NO special feedback table. The inverse is explicit rather than abstract: given (sum+lag, sum+1), recover sum = second - 1 and lag = first - sum, and it recovered all five probes including the wrapping corner (364,-364). THE PROPERTY IS REVERSIBILITY, NOT SELF-REFERENCE, and not memory either: a FORGETFUL two-word carry has it exactly as much as an append-only history would, because every component is ADD and AB2 measured ADD at zero bits erased. AI4 had to search 19,683 tables to find 216 that work; this needs nothing but addition.

entries.subject: What self-reference buys, and what actually buys the property it is asked for
entries.claim: H as a value map erases more than 3 bits, so the reversibility lives in the state rather than in what is emitted
entries.note: Eighty-one histories of length four collapse onto nine outputs, erasing 3.5944 bits by the AB measure. The state map is a bijection and the emitted value is a nine-to-one channel, at the same time and without contradiction, because they are different maps. Anyone reading only the number H produces is reading an erasing channel however well-behaved the state carrying it happens to be -- which is the distinction AB2 already drew between the accumulator reading and the pair reading, arriving here from a completely different direction.

entries.subject: What self-reference buys, and what actually buys the property it is asked for
entries.claim: the operator runs in the machine that would price it, and the implementation erases even though the mathematics does not
entries.note: programs/ladder.tasm reproduces the ladder exactly against an independent implementation, so the operator is now self-hosting in the weak sense -- expressible in the language its own ladder produces. It costs 152 instructions for nine terms and erases 6.2564 bits per instruction, which is the second-highest figure in the corpus after fold. SELF-HOSTING DOES NOT INHERIT THE REVERSIBILITY OF THE THING HOSTED: the map is a bijection and the program calls STORE on every turn of the loop, and AB2 measured STORE at the full 9.5098 bits. A reversible mathematics implemented on an erasing machine still erases, which is the gap between having a property and running it.

entries.subject: What self-reference buys, and what actually buys the property it is asked for
entries.claim: the ladder exceeds a tryte at term 15, so never forgetting is unaffordable in bounded memory
entries.note: The ladder grows like phi^n and a tryte holds -364..+364, so term 15 at 377 does not fit and fourteen do. Asked for eighteen terms the machine emits 233 then -352, wrapping rather than growing, which is the only thing bounded memory can do. THE PRICE OF A TRAJECTORY GRAPH THAT CANNOT CONVERGE IS A STATE THAT CANNOT BE BOUNDED. Every real machine erases for exactly this reason, and an implied receipt has to buy its way out of that trade rather than assume it away -- which is what AJ1 shows is possible, since reversibility gets the non-convergence without the unbounded state.

entries.subject: The smallest reversible ternary language, and the trilemma it exposes
entries.claim: the three primitive forms are a universal reversible language: every instance a permutation of order 3, generating A_27
entries.argument: Each form adds a fixed amount mod 3 to one trit under a condition on another, so three applications return every state. Order exactly 3 by construction, which is what makes the inverse derivable and an inverse instruction set unnecessary.
entries.note: All fifteen gate instances are permutations of the 27 states and every one has order exactly 3, so a program's inverse is that program with each gate applied twice more and THE LANGUAGE NEEDS NO INVERSE INSTRUCTION SET. The group they generate is A_27, agreeing with M's recorded figure from an implementation written separately -- two independent codings landing on one 28-digit number is what makes a re-implementation worth having. ERRATUM, AND THE REASON IT IS ONLY AN ERRATUM: the registration typed A_27 as a 25-digit number, dropping three zeros, so the decimal expansion in the prediction was wrong by a factor of a thousand. The tool COMPUTES 27!/2 rather than comparing against the typed digits, which is why a transcription slip in the registration is a footnote instead of a false verdict. AGENTS.md already says to derive constants and never hardcode them; the tool obeyed it and the prose did not.

entries.subject: The smallest reversible ternary language, and the trilemma it exposes
entries.claim: reversibility is inherited by composition, so every program has in-degree 1 with no analysis
entries.argument: A composition of bijections is a bijection. Every primitive is a bijection, so in-degree 1 holds for every program that can be written — the 400 sampled were a check on the implementation, never the grounds for the claim.
entries.note: Four hundred random programs of random length, and every one has in-degree exactly 1 at all 27 states with zero unreachable. A composition of bijections is a bijection, so THERE IS NOTHING A PROGRAMMER CAN WRITE IN THIS LANGUAGE THAT BREAKS IT. Compare what factor four cost everywhere else: AI4 had to search 19,683 tables to find the 216 that work, and AJ1 needed the map to be built out of addition on purpose. Here it costs no analysis, no search and no discipline -- it is a property of the alphabet rather than of the program.

entries.subject: The smallest reversible ternary language, and the trilemma it exposes
entries.claim: a straight-line reversible program costs its own length for every input, so the cost spread is exactly 1.00 and factor three is lost
entries.note: Every one of fifty straight-line programs costs exactly its own length in gates, for all 27 starting states: a spread of 1.0000. That is FLATTER THAN THE 1.02x AG1 CALLED SECURITY THEATRE, and against the 513.8x AH1 needed. Nothing in the language depends on the data, because branching on data means testing data and a test that discards its answer is erasing. So going fully reversible BUYS FACTOR FOUR AND LOSES FACTOR THREE, and the alternative registered -- that some program would show a spread above 1.00 and the worry was unfounded -- did not occur on any of them.

entries.subject: The smallest reversible ternary language, and the trilemma it exposes
entries.claim: a trilemma: in-degree one, a cost that varies, and bounded state are available two at a time and never three
entries.note: Six constructions from this corpus tabulated against the three properties, and NONE HAS ALL THREE. The reversible language has in-degree one and bounded state with a flat cost; hailstone and the three-word program have a varying cost and bounded state with trajectories that merge; and buying the first two together is Bennett's construction -- a reversible machine CAN branch on data, but only by keeping the record of which way it went, so the history grows at least one trit per branch. A thousand data-dependent steps costs 167 trytes that can never be discarded, and AJ4 already measured what happens when bounded memory meets a state that will not stop growing: it wraps at term fifteen. IN-DEGREE ONE, A COST THAT VARIES, BOUNDED STATE -- PICK TWO.

measured.hailstone_and_three_word: cost varies + bounded state, in-degree above 1
measured.history_growth: at least one trit per data-dependent step

entries.subject: The two-input ternary operations as a labelled task ladder for a grokking experiment
entries.claim: exactly 27 of the 19,683 two-input ternary operations are affine over GF(3), and 18 of the 216 reversible ones are
entries.argument: 27 = 3^3, one affine table per (alpha, beta, gamma). The 18 affine-and-reversible is 2 x 3 x 3 because alpha must be nonzero for every column to be a bijection. Parameter counting, exhaustive by construction.
entries.note: Exact. 27 = 3^3, one per (alpha, beta, gamma). The reversible count of 216 reproduces AB1 from a criterion written independently, and the 18 affine-reversible is 2 x 3 x 3 because alpha must be nonzero for every column to be a bijection -- AB1 measured that same 18 by checking affineness of tables it had already found reversible, so the two routes cross-check rather than restate. THE POINT IS THE FRACTION: the grokking literature studies a task drawn from 0.137% of this space and holds the algebraic variable fixed while sweeping everything else.

entries.subject: The two-input ternary operations as a labelled task ladder for a grokking experiment
entries.claim: affine is exactly the set a linear map can fit, and nothing else reaches a perfect fit
entries.note: Exhaustive over every (alpha,beta,gamma) and every table. Exactly 27 reach 9 of 9 rows and they are exactly the affine ones; the best any non-affine table manages is 8 of 9, and 486 of them get that close. So the label is not a convention -- it is precisely what a model with no nonlinearity can represent, and 19,656 tables need one. Modular addition, the literature task, is among the 27.

entries.subject: The two-input ternary operations as a labelled task ladder for a grokking experiment
entries.claim: all four quadrants are non-empty and the erasure varies within each
entries.note: The quadrant counts held exactly -- 18, 9, 198, 19,458, totalling 19,683 -- and the independence claim with them: reversibility and affineness really are separate axes. The variation clause FAILED, and for a reason that is itself a result. Both REVERSIBLE quadrants are pinned at exactly 1.585 bits with no spread at all, because reversible-in-the-leading-argument means every column is a bijection, so each output value appears exactly three times across the nine pairs and the erasure is log2(3) by construction. Only the erasing quadrants vary. Note also that this column measures the OUTPUT map, nine pairs onto three values, and not AB2 pair map which preserves the second argument -- the same distinction AJ2 drew, arriving again unbidden.

entries.subject: The two-input ternary operations as a labelled task ladder for a grokking experiment
entries.claim: the arena ladder is 9, 729 and 531,441 examples, and the three-trit arena is within an order of magnitude of mod-113 addition
entries.note: The counts held; the comparison failed. 729 against 12,769 is a factor of 17.5, which is not within an order of magnitude however generously read -- the canonical setup sits BETWEEN the three-trit arena and the six-trit one rather than beside either. The ladder still brackets it, which is what an experiment needs, but the sentence claimed something tidier than the arithmetic supports and the arithmetic was available before the claim was written.

entries.subject: Does the algebra of a task predict when a network generalises? A grokking sweep with the algebraic label as the variable
entries.claim: grokking reproduces on this task family at all, with a gap of at least 5x between memorisation and generalisation
entries.note: Held with room to spare. Both reversible tasks memorise 292 training pairs by step 200 and do not reach 90% on the 437 held-out pairs until thousands of steps later -- gaps of 36x and 19x against a predicted 5x. So the phenomenon reproduces on a family that is NOT modular arithmetic, and whose hidden structure is a base-three FACTORISATION rather than a Fourier basis: the network sees a and b as opaque tokens in 0..26 and has to discover that the operation is positionwise in base three.

entries.subject: Does the algebra of a task predict when a network generalises? A grokking sweep with the algebraic label as the variable
entries.claim: the affine task groks soonest, so the algebraic label predicts the outcome
entries.note: FAILED, and it inverted rather than merely missing. The AFFINE task -- ternary modular addition, which is what the grokking literature studies almost exclusively -- is the SLOWER of the two on every paired seed, with a median of 10,800 steps against 6,200, and on one seed it never reached 90% at all inside a 40,000-step budget while the non-affine task generalised on all five. Run once this would be a draw; run five times with everything but the algebra held fixed it is a direction. THE CANONICAL GROKKING TASK IS HARDER THAN A NON-AFFINE SIBLING, which is a comparison the literature has not been able to make because it has no labelled task ladder to make it on. Stated limit: one table per quadrant, so this measures seed-stability and not table-stability, and sweeping tables within a quadrant is the obvious next thing. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE CRITERION IS A COIN. As registered this is ONE paired comparison -- same architecture, optimiser, split and step budget -- so P(the null crosses the line) is 50%, and the recorded FAILED could have been a HELD on the toss. THE FINDING SURVIVES AND IS MATERIALLY STRONGER THAN THE CRITERION ASKED FOR, which is the whole reason the two must be disclosed apart: the run's own five seeds put the non-affine task faster in 4 OF 4 PAIRED SEEDS, medians 10,800 against 6,200, with the affine task failing to generalise inside 40,000 steps on one of five and the non-affine on none of five. This note already said "run once this would be a draw"; what is new is that the registered line was the run-once version and the evidence is the five-seed version. The outcome stands as recorded. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

entries.subject: Does the algebra of a task predict when a network generalises? A grokking sweep with the algebraic label as the variable
entries.claim: the erasing tasks have a majority-class baseline above 40% while the reversible ones sit near 3.7%
entries.note: FAILED, and the reasoning behind it was the error. I conflated "erases in the leading argument" with "has a skewed output distribution", and they are different properties. The affine-erasing table is f = b, which is a BIJECTION in its second argument, so its outputs are perfectly uniform and its baseline is 0.0457 -- identical to the reversible tasks. Only tritwise MIN is genuinely skewed, at 0.1918, and even that is far short of 40%. AL3 had already shown the erasure column for that quadrant spans 1.585 to 3.170 and the table chosen sat at the uniform end, so the information needed to avoid this was on the record before the prediction was written.

entries.subject: Does the algebra of a task predict when a network generalises? A grokking sweep with the algebraic label as the variable
entries.claim: the affine-erasing quadrant is degenerate and is learned within a tenth of the steps the affine-reversible task needs
entries.note: Held at 0.028 against a predicted tenth: 200 steps versus 7,200, with no memorisation-to-generalisation gap at all. And it is degenerate BY PROOF rather than by luck -- an affine table is reversible in its leading argument exactly when alpha is nonzero, so affine AND erasing forces alpha = 0 and the function ignores its first input entirely. All nine tables in that quadrant are one-input functions, so the prediction covers the quadrant and not just the table trained.

entries.subject: Does a purpose-built search puzzle have the find-against-verify asymmetry? A ternary proof-of-work candidate, exhaustive over all 531,441 message-nonce pairs
entries.claim: the variance of hit counts across messages separates a compressing puzzle from a relabelling, landing within 25% of binomial at every difficulty while a bijective candidate gives exactly zero
entries.note: FAILED at two of six difficulties, and the failure is the whole result. Two of the three legs held: the mean first hit sat within 15% of the finite-population null at every k, and both bijective controls gave a hit-count variance of EXACTLY zero against a binomial 12.73 -- which is the discriminator D4 could not supply, since truncating any permutation gives perfectly uniform buckets and a collision count therefore cannot separate a hash from a relabelling. The leg that failed is the one that mattered. The candidate came in at 0.729x and 0.674x of binomial at k = 1 and k = 2, MORE uniform than chance, and a puzzle more uniform than chance is structured. Chasing that deviation found the structure (see F-MESSAGE-COMMUTES-OUT-OF-A-GROUP-FEEDFORWARD). The registration said in advance that agreement would not be a certificate and that only disagreement could refute; the disagreement arrived and did exactly that.

entries.subject: Does a purpose-built search puzzle have the find-against-verify asymmetry? A ternary proof-of-work candidate, exhaustive over all 531,441 message-nonce pairs
entries.claim: the tabulator kills a bijective puzzle and the algebra kills an affine one, both at one operation per solve, with affine strictly worse because it needs no table
entries.note: Held on every clause. AD2 tabulated a program to price it and broke even at seventy queries; here the same attack breaks a bijective puzzle outright at one lookup, because a permutation can be walked backwards from the target. The affine candidate is strictly worse: the nonce is a rotation of a difference, so there is nothing to precompute but a single 6x6 inversion and the attack is profitable on query one. The gap between the two is exactly the 729-entry table. So the two algebraic labels this project has carried since AL are, for a puzzle, both disqualifying -- and in a strict order.

entries.subject: Does a purpose-built search puzzle have the find-against-verify asymmetry? A ternary proof-of-work candidate, exhaustive over all 531,441 message-nonce pairs
entries.claim: a puzzle that is non-invertible in the nonce strands messages at the null rate, and a bijective one strands none
entries.note: Held, and it is the symmetric twin of the receipt result. The receipt died needing in-degree one; the puzzle NEEDS in-degree above one, or AN2(a) inverts it -- and pays for that in messages no nonce can mine. At maximum difficulty 264 of 729 messages, 36.2%, have no solution at all, and a miner holding one grinds forever. Both bijective controls strand exactly zero, so the property that guarantees every message is mineable is the same property that lets an attacker skip the mining. The number survives the keyed reconstruction (35 and 283), which is what shows the result is about compression rather than about this particular construction.

entries.subject: Does a purpose-built search puzzle have the find-against-verify asymmetry? A ternary proof-of-work candidate, exhaustive over all 531,441 message-nonce pairs
entries.claim: widening the nonce cures the stranding and the understated work at once, because both are one symptom of the nonce space failing to outrun the target rarity
entries.note: Held on both halves, and they moved together. A twelve-trit nonce absorbed in two blocks through the same compression function strands nothing at maximum difficulty and raises the mean search from 311.2 to 735.0, which is within 0.8% of 3^6 = 729 -- the figure a proper lottery owes and the one a truncated nonce space understates by 58%. So AN3 is not a fact about irreversibility as such but about a nonce space too small for the target, and the design rule is measured rather than borrowed: nonce space must exceed target rarity by orders of magnitude. That is what the extraNonce field in Bitcoin is for.

entries.subject: Can an erasing machine certify that a secret was wiped? Ceremony maps over 729 secrets, and whether the erasure measure is the right certificate
entries.claim: the pseudorandom ceremony map measures E within 5% of the 0.8265 null while exposing, within 10% of 268, secrets whose preimage is a single point
entries.note: FAILED on the erasure clause and held on the one that carried the argument, and the post-mortem is worth more than either. E came in at 0.8894 against a null of 0.8265 -- 7.6% out where 5% was registered. Sweeping 400 pseudorandom maps then showed the null was exactly right (mean 0.8269, sd 0.0299) and that 336 of 400 draws WOULD have passed the 5% band. The band was reasonable; the draw was not. This set fixed one seed as its control and happened to fix a 2.09-sigma one, so the failure is about the sample and not about the criterion or the claim. A SINGLE FIXED PSEUDORANDOM MAP CANNOT BE SCORED AGAINST A DISTRIBUTIONAL NULL: it is one sample and the null is a spread. The exposed clause survived on the same unlucky draw only because it was given a 10% band rather than a 5% one. And the substance held completely: 252 of 729 secrets, 34.6%, are recovered EXACTLY from the public output while the average erasure reads healthy at 0.89 bits. E is a mean and hiding is a minimum. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE FAILING LEG IS NOT DISCRIMINATING. AO1(a)'s 5% band around the 0.8265 null is crossed by the NULL ITSELF about 16% of the time -- the tool's own 400 draws put 336 inside the band and 64 outside -- so the recorded FAILED is a draw the registered run happened to take and not a refutation of anything. THE VERDICT IS CORRUPTED AND THE FINDING IS NOT, and they have to be said separately: the substance here is a direct count rather than a comparison against a band -- 252 of 729 secrets, 34.6%, recovered EXACTLY from the public output while the average erasure reads a healthy 0.89 bits, so E is a mean and hiding is a minimum -- and AO1(b), scored on the same frozen map, is discriminating at a 3.77% crossing rate. One limit on this disclosure: the methodological rule the failure produced -- a single fixed pseudorandom object is one sample and a null is a distribution -- is the product of the POST-HOC 400-draw sweep, not of the registered run. The outcome stands as recorded. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

measured.control_draw_position: 2.09 sd from the mean of 400 draws

entries.subject: Can an erasing machine certify that a secret was wiped? Ceremony maps over 729 secrets, and whether the erasure measure is the right certificate
entries.claim: truncating the mixer to m trits gives every output exactly 3^(6-m) preimages, minimum equal to maximum, while the pseudorandom map has a minimum of 1
entries.argument: The mixer is a bijection, so the 729 secrets land on 729 distinct values; grouping those by their low m trits partitions them into 3^m classes of exactly 3^(6-m). Flatness is forced by the pigeonhole equality, not observed -- and it holds at every width where the truncation divides the space.
entries.note: Held exactly at every m from 1 to 5. The point is the reuse: D4 FAILED because truncating any permutation gives perfectly uniform buckets, which made a collision count useless as evidence of mixing. That same forced uniformity is precisely what a wipe wants -- every secret hidden among exactly as many others as every other secret, with no output easier to invert than another. A construction disqualified as a hash test is the right answer to a different question, and the disqualifying property IS the qualifying one.

entries.subject: Can an erasing machine certify that a secret was wiped? Ceremony maps over 729 secrets, and whether the erasure measure is the right certificate
entries.claim: truncation attains the pigeonhole hiding bound at every power of three and the pseudorandom map attains it nowhere
entries.note: Held on both clauses. The bound itself is arithmetic -- every preimage of at least h forces an image of at most floor(729/h) -- so what was at risk was attainment, and the split is total: truncation attains it at all four, the pseudorandom map at none, and not one of 400 random draws is even flat. A balanced wipe does not happen by accident. The exchange rate is the useful number: to hide every secret among 27 others the public output may carry 4.755 of its 9.510 bits, so HIDING IS BOUGHT WITH OUTPUT BITS at a fixed price, and a ceremony whose parameters must be large enough to be useful cannot buy much of it.

entries.subject: Can an erasing machine certify that a secret was wiped? Ceremony maps over 729 secrets, and whether the erasure measure is the right certificate
entries.claim: the count of fully-exposed secrets lands within 10% of both the 268 null and AN3's measured 264 stranded blocks, because both are tails of the same Poisson(1)
entries.note: Held on both comparisons. A block with no winning nonce and a secret with a unique preimage are the k=0 and k=1 tails of the same Poisson(1), and Poisson(1) puts identical mass on those two, so the counts are equal by construction rather than by coincidence. AN3 measured 264 unmineable blocks; AO measures 252 unhidden secrets; the shared null is 268. Two results this project reached by different routes, four sets apart, are the same number, and neither set knew it. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: AO4 IS NOT DISCRIMINATING, and the tool's own prose said so while the manifest recorded a clean HELD. Over 8,000 draws of a random map on 729 points at the tool's own seeding the null is modal 268, mean 268.47, sd 12.98, central 95% [243, 294]; the measured 252 sits 1.27 sd INSIDE it. P(the null misses either of the two registered bands, which is what this leg requires) = 6.54%, CI [6.02, 7.10]. The tool already wrote that this is "the SAME map, scored against a 10% band instead of a 5% one, and that is the only reason AO4 held where AO1 failed" -- so the set knew, and the class tally did not. The structural point the note below makes, that two tails of one Poisson(1) carry identical mass, is an argument and stands on its own. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

measured.reason: P(Poisson(1)=0) = P(Poisson(1)=1) = 1/e, so the two tails are equal by construction

entries.subject: Can a hash-only key layer give a minted coin an owner? Lamport one-time signatures at base two and base three, exhaustive over 729 messages
entries.claim: an attacker holding one valid signature can forge exactly one message, the one already signed
entries.note: Held exhaustively. Every one of the 729 signed messages forges exactly itself and nothing else, so the scheme is not broken at first use -- which is the assumption everything else in the set rests on. The controls pin both ends of the meter: holding no signature forges nothing, holding all of them forges everything.

entries.subject: Can a hash-only key layer give a minted coin an owner? Lamport one-time signatures at base two and base three, exhaustive over 729 messages
entries.claim: two signatures under one key leak at the binomial rate, mean within 5% of 21.43, maximum 64 and minimum 1
entries.note: Held on all three clauses, and the mean agrees with the closed form to one part in ten thousand -- which is the real content, because it confirms the binomial model is the right description of what a reused key gives away rather than merely a plausible one. The one-time restriction is therefore not advisory: a second signature under the same key hands away 2.94% of the message space on average and 8.78% at worst, and there is no configuration in which it hands away nothing unless the same message is signed twice. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: ALL THREE OF THIS PREDICTION'S LEGS CANNOT GO THE OTHER WAY. (a) the base-3 digit map is a bijection onto (Z_3)^6 and the six positions are independent under a uniform pair, so the forgeable count is exactly 2^k and the exhaustive mean over all 531,441 ordered pairs is IDENTICALLY (1 + 2/3)^6 -- 11390625/531441 = 21.43347050754458 against (5/3)^6 = 21.433470507544587, a difference of -7.1e-15. (b) the maximum 64 is attained by any two messages differing in all six positions, witness forgeable({0, 728}). (c) the minimum 1 is attained by a message paired with itself, witness forgeable({0, 0}). NOTE PRECISELY WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is not the decoration F-REGISTRATION-IS-NOT-RISK scored for, because the run computed something the registration had not stated; what it could not do is come out otherwise. `at_risk` is left as registered -- moving it would be a re-audit, and this sweep re-scores nothing. The set's own summary already says two of its four "should not have been registered". See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

measured.maximum_is: 2^6, when the messages differ in all six positions
measured.minimum_is: signing the same message twice, which reveals nothing new

entries.subject: Can a hash-only key layer give a minted coin an owner? Lamport one-time signatures at base two and base three, exhaustive over 729 messages
entries.claim: ternary leaks less of its own space than binary on key reuse, 2.94% against 5.63%
entries.note: Held, including the mechanism clause -- ternary digits collide more often and leak less anyway, because six positions against ten outweighs two thirds against one half. But it should not have been registered. Both sides are the closed form (1 + (b-1)/b)^pos and the registration itself computed both before the run, so nothing here was ever at risk. AGENTS.md names this failure directly: inflating the registered set with facts that were never at risk turns the discipline into decoration. Recorded as held and as a registration that should not have been made.

measured.mechanism: trits differ with p = 2/3 against bits at 1/2, so the per-position rate is HIGHER for ternary and the leak is still lower, because the position count falls faster

entries.subject: Can a hash-only key layer give a minted coin an owner? Lamport one-time signatures at base two and base three, exhaustive over 729 messages
entries.claim: ternary pays for that advantage in destruction: 12 of 18 preimages against 10 of 20, and strictly more erased bits
entries.note: Held. The wipe is a projection from a b-tuple of preimages onto the one revealed, and AB's own erasure measure agrees with the closed form log2(ALPHA^(b-1)) exactly, so the ternary key destroys 19.020 bits of material against binary's 15.850. AP3's leak advantage is bought with a larger wipe, and AO already priced what a wipe costs. Like AP3 this was arithmetic before it was measured: (b-1)/b and the projection erasure are both closed forms, and the only thing genuinely measured was that erasureOf agrees with them.

entries.subject: How wide should an authenticated tree be, and does a power of three ever beat a power of two? A cost model over every integer branching factor from 2 to 1024, 45 leaf counts, and a bytes-per-verify-operation exchange rate swept across eight decades
entries.claim: binary is never optimal for a vector commitment, the optimum never descends past three, and across the swept leaf counts THREE is the large-gamma optimum more often than four
entries.note: Failed on its last clause, and that clause was the whole point. The first three parts held exactly: no cell in 2,880 has argmin 2, the optimum never goes below 3, and it never widens as verifying gets dearer. But three does not beat four at the verify-dominated limit -- it TIES, 21 leaf counts each. Chasing the tie produced F-TREE-BRANCHES-IN-ITS-OWN-BASE, which is a better answer than the one predicted: 3^k leaf counts want three and 2^k leaf counts want four, so the tie was a property of how many of each shape this sweep contains rather than of trees. T-CLAIM-NARROWED-BY-A-DESIGN, fourth bite. NARROWED AFTERWARDS, AND STATED HERE SO A READER OF AQ ALONE IS NOT MISLED: AR4 lifted the constant-arity constraint every tree in this sweep was built under, and F-TREE-BRANCHES-IN-ITS-OWN-BASE turned out to be a property of CONSTANT trees rather than of trees. 25 of these 45 leaf counts change shape once radix sequences are admitted, 11 of the 18 powers of three among them, and N = 729 wants [4,4,4,4,3] rather than six threes -- for 0.0178% of the total cost, a surface flat to four decimal places. AR's evidence for that is FREQUENCY and not magnitude: its null over 100 redraws has a tail reaching 23.7%, ABOVE the subject's own worst cell, so a structureless per-level cost can produce a larger maximum than the real regime does, while the frequency of improvement separates a hundredfold. T-CLAIM-NARROWED-BY-A-DESIGN, fifth bite, and the second time the class has bitten this same sentence.

entries.subject: How wide should an authenticated tree be, and does a power of three ever beat a power of two? A cost model over every integer branching factor from 2 to 1024, 45 leaf counts, and a bytes-per-verify-operation exchange rate swept across eight decades
entries.claim: counting cells whose cost-minimising branching factor is a power of three against those where it is a power of two, three takes strictly more, despite ten powers of two being in range against six of three
entries.note: The handicap was real and the geometry did not overcome it: two takes 1,044 cells to three's 821. But PER ARITY IN RANGE the ordering reverses -- each power of three wins 137 cells against each power of two's 104 -- so the registered wording measured how many of each arity I put in the sweep as much as it measured the trees. The claim was answerable only because a design decision had already half-decided it.

entries.subject: How wide should an authenticated tree be, and does a power of three ever beat a power of two? A cost model over every integer branching factor from 2 to 1024, 45 leaf counts, and a bytes-per-verify-operation exchange rate swept across eight decades
entries.claim: unit invariance FAILS: recomputing every cost in whole trytes rather than whole bytes moves at least one argmin, because a proof travels in whole units and that rounding is a ceiling a bare scale factor is not
entries.note: Held, registered deliberately against the obvious answer that a scale factor cannot move an argmin. Eight cells of 2,880 flip, all of them near-ties between adjacent arities, exactly as the argument said they would. It held for the right reason on an effect thirteen times smaller than the instrument first reported: the registered conversion divided a COUNT OF OPERATIONS by bytes-per-tryte and rounded it, a category error twice over, and showed 103. Caught before scoring because a 19% unit change cannot honestly move an optimum from three to six. T-INSTRUMENT-FALSE-VERDICT, eighteenth bite. The wrong conversion is kept in the tool and both numbers are pinned, so the fix cannot silently regress.

entries.subject: How wide should an authenticated tree be, and does a power of three ever beat a power of two? A cost model over every integer branching factor from 2 to 1024, 45 leaf counts, and a bytes-per-verify-operation exchange rate swept across eight decades
entries.claim: at every cell where either arity is within 15% of that cell's optimum, the totals at branching factor 64 and 256 differ by no more than 15%
entries.note: Failed and not narrowly -- 571 of 909, worst case 149%. But 426 of those 571 are cells where 64 and 256 sit at DIFFERENT DEPTHS, and when 256 saves a whole level it wins by that level while when it does not it pays four times the verify for nothing. So the two are close to interchangeable at a fixed depth and completely different across a depth step, which makes the answer a fact about the leaf count rather than about either arity. entries.claim: letting the arity vary is worth less than a sixth: at every cell of both vector-regime sweeps the best radix sequence costs at least 85% of the best constant arity's cost
entries.note: Held, and the bound is worth less than it looks. The worst cell in 68,408 is 12.30% at N = 257 and the worst on AQ's own grid is 9.99% at N = 128, both inside the registered 15%. But the post-hoc null over 100 redraws has a TAIL reaching 23.7%, above the subject's worst cell, so a structureless per-level cost can produce a larger maximum than the real regime does and magnitude discriminates nothing here. What discriminates is frequency, which is AR3. The line's placement decided this verdict: a 10% line would have FAILED at 12.30%, and the reason for widening it to 15% -- a hand case at 9.99% that would have made 10% a coin toss -- was on the record before the run. T-CRITERION-IN-THE-NOISE applied before the fact rather than after it. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: AR1 IS NOT DISCRIMINATING AS A RATE, which is new and is not what this note already discloses. The 23.7% tail recorded below says the MAGNITUDE discriminates nothing. Drawn MATCHED to the subject's own cell set -- 300 redraws over [2, 8192] x 8 decades -- the null crosses the registered 15% line 9.0% of the time, CI [6.3, 12.8], and crosses the measured 12.30% 14.0% of the time. THE DENOMINATOR IS THE WHOLE STORY and it is this audit's sharpest transferable lesson: the same null over 6 leaf counts crosses 0.4% of the time and over 8,191 leaves at a single gamma 0.5%, so a maximum over six cells and a maximum over 65,528 cells are DIFFERENT STATISTICS and a null drawn at the wrong one flatters the line. Both maxima land at N = 1024, which the registration did not require and could not assume -- had they sat at different leaf counts the ratio would have compared two unrelated extremes. The unregistered robustness windows show the statistic is not universal: over [8192, 16384] the CONSTANT cost is perfectly flat, because 4^7 = 16384 covers the whole octave, so the constant tree pays a fixed premium for a full-size tree while the varying tree tracks the leaf count and is therefore both cheaper and raggeder. Tightness against the ceiling is bought with raggedness. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: AR2 IS NOT DISCRIMINATING AND NOTHING HAD SAID SO -- but it is the minority-outcome sub-type, and the direction matters. The matched null's jump ratio has p10 0.500, median 0.769 and maximum 44.06 over the 32 of 500 draws where a jump exists at all, so P(the null crosses the 0.5 line) = 87.5%, CI [71.9, 95.0]. The measured 0.334 is therefore inside the noise -- AND THE RECORDED HELD IS THE NULL'S MINORITY OUTCOME, so the leg still carries about three bits: the line is in the noise and the run beat the odds, which is a different thing from a line the null clears routinely in the direction recorded. entries.note: Held, and it is the one the registration said could not be called. 6,144 of 7,169 leaf counts -- 85.7% -- have a strictly cheaper varying optimum, against a null of 0.83% of draw-by-leaf pairs: a hundredfold separation, and the statistic that actually shows the effect is structure rather than arithmetic. I registered the reasoning against my own hand sample and the reasoning was right; the sample was drawn at powers, which is where a constant tree is at its best. The unhelped 1,025 are EXACTLY the leaf counts whose optimal tree is a constant arity, with no exceptions in 7,169 -- and those are powers of FOUR rather than powers in general, since four is the arity the optimum wants. 2187 = 3^7 is helped. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE CLASSIFICATION OF THIS LEG IS ITSELF UNDETERMINED, which is a fitting answer for the prediction whose registration said it could not be called. A matched null over the registered deep window at 500 draws crosses the 50% line 4.2% of the time, CI [2.8, 6.3] -- an interval that STRADDLES the 5% bar this audit scored against, so what is undecided is the classification and not the measurement. The null is bimodal: 469 of 500 draws are degenerate and 21 of the remaining 31 cross, so CONDITIONAL ON THE NULL NOT BEING DEGENERATE IT CROSSES 68% OF THE TIME. The criterion therefore separates degenerate cost tables from non-degenerate ones rather than structure from noise -- and the frozen control this set registered WAS degenerate, which is the second bite of T-CONTROL-CANNOT-DISCRIMINATE seen from a new angle. 2,000 draws would settle it and were not run. entries.claim: the optimal tree gets deeper more often than shallower: over the deep contiguous window at the verify-dominated rate, leaf counts whose varying optimum is strictly deeper than their constant optimum outnumber those whose varying optimum is strictly shallower
entries.note: FAILED, and inverted rather than narrowly missed: 3,580 shallower against 2,176 deeper, 1.6 to 1. The registered reasoning had the mechanism backwards. It argued that more levels means more per-level slack to exploit, so the tree should grow. What a sequence actually buys is the SAME verify budget in FEWER levels: the quantity gamma is charged on is never larger than the constant tree's, it is identical at 2,861 of 7,169 leaf counts, and 1,836 of the 3,580 shallower cells are of exactly that kind. THE SLACK REMOVES A LEVEL RATHER THAN ADDING ONE, and the saving there is level overhead rather than work. That mechanism is what overturns AQ's headline: 25 of AQ's 45 leaf counts change shape, 11 of the 18 powers of three among them, and N = 729 wants [4,4,4,4,3] rather than six threes -- for 0.0178% of the total cost. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE CRITERION CANNOT GO THE OTHER WAY, and this one is the auditor's flagged judgement call. A matched null over 500 redraws fails this leg 500 times out of 500, CI [99.2, 100], so the recorded FAILED carries no information as a comparison against chance. But 489 of those 500 draws are DEGENERATE -- one arity optimal everywhere, so no depth ever moves and "deeper outnumber shallower" is trivially false -- and of the 31 non-degenerate draws none holds the leg, CI [0, 11%]. A reader could reasonably say the degeneracy makes that the wrong null, and the doubt is recorded rather than resolved. THE FINDING DOES NOT REST ON THE NULL AT ALL: it rests on the subject's own deterministic counts -- 3,580 shallower against 2,176 deeper, the verify budget identical at 2,861 of 7,169 leaf counts and 1,836 of the 3,580 shallower cells sitting at exactly that identical budget -- from which the mechanism follows and AQ's headline is overturned. The outcome stands as recorded. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

entries.subject: Does the mixer's residual algebra help a ledger forger? Four designed attacks on D's split-round chain as a ledger head -- a cross-ledger census of the compensating family over 2,000 drawn ledgers, the differential table of g = P - I, a delta ordering built from it, and a meet-in-the-middle join over four modified entries -- each priced in a cost model stated before the run
entries.claim: the 26 is a fact about the mixer and not about one ledger, and there is no weak ledger class: over 2,000 independently drawn six-entry ledgers swept over all 10,920 distinct compensating forgeries each, the mean accept count lands within 0.6 of the chance value 14.979, the variance-to-mean ratio lands in [0.80, 1.25], and no single ledger accepts more than 40
entries.note: Held on all three legs. The mean is 1.5 standard errors above chance, the dispersion is Poisson to within 2%, and the worst of 2,000 ledgers accepts 30 against a line at 40. The 17% preimage spread F-MIXER-HEAD-IS-NOT-FLAT measured at length two does NOT reach the six-entry forgery neighbourhood: had it, the registered arithmetic put the ratio at 1.43 and the line at 1.25 would have fired. Two further structural cuts were looked at and neither is a lever -- no merge distance and no carry pattern accepts above 1.05x chance, so the arithmetic-versus-tritwise group mismatch that a forger might have exploited buys nothing at this width. What this does NOT say is that the 26 was a good number to publish: the published sweep counts every forgery twice, so 26 of 21,840 is 13 of 10,920 (F-COMPENSATING-SWEEP-DOUBLE-COUNTS), and 13 against 14.979 is 0.5 sd low rather than the 13% deficit the ordered pair suggests.

entries.claim: there is no strong differential in the residual algebra: the differential table of g over GF(3)^6, over all 728 non-zero input differences and all 729 output differences, has a maximum cell of at most 27, so no input-to-output difference through g holds with probability better than 1/27
entries.note: Held, and by a wider margin than the registration expected: the maximum is 8, not merely under 27. The Feistel's free two-round characteristic -- probability one in the mod-27 group, four windows in eight rounds -- does not survive into the tritwise metric at all, which is the mechanism the registration named as the way this could fail by an order of magnitude. The number that makes the verdict readable is the control: over twelve random permutations the same statistic runs 7 to 9 and the empty-cell fraction 36.81% against g's 36.74%, so g's differential behaviour is not distinguishable from a random permutation's residual. ONE DISCLOSURE. The registration's own null arithmetic put a random function's maximum at 9 to 11; the measured controls say 7 to 9. The null was slightly wrong, it was arithmetic rather than measurement, and it decided nothing, because the line was at 27 and the answer was 8. The affine control returning exactly 729 is what says the statistic could have reached the hundreds.

entries.claim: the meet-in-the-middle join does not beat its own ideal yield: the four-position join returns between 0.97 and 1.10 times the ideal 531,441 forgeries, on the canonical ledger and on every one of eight independently drawn ones
entries.note: Held, and it was the one the registration said could not be called. The two half-tables are genuinely sparse -- 335,881 and 335,763 of 531,441 keys occupied, meeting on 212,371 -- so the failure mode was live: had their reachable key sets coincided the join would have returned the sum of squared counts, which the tool measures at 2.0003 for this very table. It returns 1.0020 instead. The non-flatness F-MIXER-HEAD-IS-NOT-FLAT found is real and is NOT cashable here, and a chain built on a random permutation gives 1.0000, so the mixer's structure buys the forger nothing in yield. The value of the result is what it licenses: the join is a complete enumeration of the four-position family at 6.99 ops per forgery, and that is the cost figure the ledger question actually turns on.

entries.subject: Does the mixer's residual algebra help a ledger forger? Four designed attacks on D's split-round chain as a ledger head -- a cross-ledger census of the compensating family over 2,000 drawn ledgers, the differential table of g = P - I, a delta ordering built from it, and a meet-in-the-middle join over four modified entries -- each priced in a cost model stated before the run
entries.claim: ordering deltas by the differential table more than halves the forger's trials: over the same 2,000 ledgers, restricted to the five adjacent position pairs and to cases where at least one of the 728 deltas is accepted, the mean rank of the first accepted delta under a differential-table-descending order with ties broken uniformly is less than 0.5 times the mean rank under a uniformly random order
entries.note: Held at 0.4506 against a line at 0.5, and the margin needed a spread beside it rather than a point: the bootstrap 95% interval is [0.4425, 0.4589] and two further seeds give 0.4495 and 0.4566, none of them reaching the line. AN1's finding -- that this mixer's hit variance came in LOW, more uniform than chance -- was the registered route to failure and it did not transfer: g's differential table is as heavy-tailed as a random function's, with 8.01% of cells holding three or more and those cells carrying 26.4% of the mass, against the 26.4% the Poisson null predicts. THE MECHANISM IS EXACT AND IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE SET. An accepted forgery at an adjacent pair IS the realisation of a two-round differential, so a delta whose cell is empty cannot be accepted -- 0 accepts in 2,669,929 tries -- and the accept rate rises linearly with the cell, 0.98x chance at cell one to 6.65x at cell seven. A forger with the 531,441-entry table discards 36.67% of the family with certainty and finds the top 8.04% carrying 26.86% of the accepts.

entries.subject: What does an INSERTION cost a ledger forger? Set AS left the route open by naming it: P has one fixed point, so from every accumulator exactly one entry value leaves the mixer head unchanged, and every forgery in AS keeps the ledger at six entries. This set prices a forger who may lengthen it -- insert, delete and rearrange against a ledger publishing BOTH heads -- in two currencies stated before the run, operations and GROWTH, with no exchange rate invented between them
entries.claim: insertion is paid for in LENGTH and the length is single digits: over 2,000 independently drawn six-entry ledgers, the minimum number of forced no-op insertions that restores BOTH heads, computed exactly by breadth-first search over Z_729 on that ledger's seven forced generators, has a mean in [4.0, 6.0] and no single ledger of the 2,000 needs more than 12
entries.note: Held on both legs, at 4.934 against a registered band of [4.0, 6.0] and a worst ledger of 10 against a line at 12. Neither named failure route fired. The uniform-generator null measures 4.966 and a chain built on a random permutation 4.911, so THE SEVEN FORCED VALUES ARE NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM SEVEN INDEPENDENT UNIFORM DRAWS at this length -- g's image being 465 of 729 does not compound into a shrinking support the way the registration feared. The order census looks like structure and is not: 414.96 per 729 at order 729 against a null 486 is entirely the gap-0 generator counted once per ledger, since that one generator is the same constant on all 2,000 and has order 243. Remove it and the other 12,000 gaps give (4708 - 2000)/12000 = 0.2257 against a null 0.2222 and 7969/12000 = 0.664 against 0.6667. THE INTERESTING END IS THE LEFT ONE: 18 of the 2,000 ledgers have a minimum of 1, and those are exactly the chains that stand on the fixed point u* at some gap, where the forced no-op is arithmetically zero and a SINGLE inserted entry forges both heads. What this does not price is a forger who inserts values that are NOT no-ops; that forger needs two entries on every ledger and no search at all, which is F-A-UNIVERSAL-TWO-ENTRY-INSERTION-FORGERY and not this prediction. DISCLOSURE ADDED AFTER THE FACT, AND THE OUTCOME IS NOT CHANGED. Set AU's F-A-LINE-IN-THE-NOISE-THAT-PASSES-IS-THE-SAME-DEFECT says a criterion sitting in the noise leaves no signal when it lands INSIDE its band, so the corpus records this defect only when it happens to fail. Applied to AT1's own maximum leg, it fires. The line was at 12 and the measurement was 10; the uniform null's most likely maximum over 2,000 draws IS 10, at probability 0.33, and P(a 2,000-draw null maximum exceeds 10) = 0.29, exceeds 11 = 0.12, exceeds 12 = 0.077 with a 95% interval of [0.044, 0.109] from 500,000 draws carrying 20 exceedances. Re-run at twelve seeds the subject's own maximum spans [9, 13] and CROSSES THE REGISTERED LINE AT TWO OF THEM. So the leg was not measuring the subject: its measured value is the null's modal outcome and its line sits one step above where chance lands anyway. AT1 STAYS HELD -- the registered run is the run, and an outcome fixed at the results commit is the only property of this record a later edit cannot fake. What changes is what the leg is worth as evidence, which is nothing. See F-THE-BITE-COUNT-IS-WHAT-FAILED-NOT-WHAT-HAPPENED, and note that AT1(a)'s mean leg is 31.4 standard errors from its nearest band edge and AT4's maximum leg fires at none of the twelve, so this is a diagnosis and not a blanket. AND THE CORPUS-WIDE SWEEP THIS ENTRY ASKED FOR HAS NOW BEEN RUN. AT1(b) is confirmed not discriminating at a 7.7% crossing rate with 2 of 12 seeds over the line, and AT1(a) is confirmed discriminating at 31.4 standard errors, so the diagnosis below survives contact with a null drawn independently of it. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

entries.claim: and that is not a property of length six: over ledger lengths 2 through 12 with 2,000 independently drawn ledgers at each length, the mean minimum insertion count is strictly decreasing at every one of the ten steps, lies above 9.0 at length two and below 4.5 at length twelve, and no single ledger at any length needs more than 100 insertions
entries.note: FAILED, on the third leg alone, and the failure is arithmetic I did myself rather than anything about the mixer. Three legs held: the mean is strictly decreasing at every one of the ten steps, 13.592 at length two is above 9.0, and 3.3625 at length twelve is below 4.5 -- and the whole curve tracks the uniform-generator null -- within 0.64 at length two and within 0.17 from length three on -- so a longer ledger really is cheaper to forge by insertion and it is cheaper for the counting reason and not a structural one. The fourth leg registered a bound on a MAXIMUM using a heuristic that is only about a MEAN. The exponential approximation that predicts 4.87 at length six -- accurate to 0.03 there -- puts the probability of a length-two ledger needing more than 100 insertions at essentially zero. Drawn directly, the uniform null exceeds 100 in 22, 25 and 33 of 50,000 draws at three seeds, so 2,000 draws expect about one and the line had roughly a 58% chance of firing on the null alone. The measured worst is 146; the null's own maximum over 50,000 draws is 243 at every seed. SO THE SUBJECT'S TAIL IS NOT HEAVIER THAN CHANCE and no claim is made that it is -- 146 against a single-draw null maximum of 81 is two samples from the same heavy tail. The lesson is the general one: a heuristic that is right about a mean can be wrong about a maximum by an order of magnitude, because the tail of this problem is governed by the cyclic subgroup a bad generator set generates rather than by counting multisets. T-CRITERION-IN-THE-NOISE, fourth bite. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE FAILING LEG IS NOT DISCRIMINATING. AT2(d)'s bound on the maximum had roughly a 58% chance of firing on the null alone, so the recorded FAILED is a coin. entries.claim: insertion has free parameters and deletion has none: over 2,000 drawn six-entry ledgers, (a) the two-free-insertion family -- 28 gap pairs p <= q, the first value free over all 729 and the second forced by the arithmetic total, so 20,412 candidates and a chance yield of 28.0 -- accepts with a mean within 2.0 of 28.0 and a variance-to-mean ratio in [0.80, 1.25]; and (b) at most 3 of the 2,000 ledgers admit any deletion-only forgery over all 63 non-empty subsets of their entries, against a chance expectation of 0.237 ledgers
entries.note: FAILED on half (a) by 0.012, and the miss is a real effect rather than a line flipped by noise: 30.0120 against 28.0 is seventeen standard errors, not a coin. The LINE was fine; the CHANCE VALUE was wrong, and the fact that makes it wrong was written into this set's own registration two hundred lines above the prediction. I4 says gap zero is the tritwise identity on every ledger. At a same-gap pair the map x -> STEP[STEP[a][x]][-x] is a composition of two bijections in the accumulator, so it is a PERMUTATION for every x, and the pair is accepted exactly when a is one of its fixed points; summed over all 729 accumulators that is 741, a mean of 1.0165, which is where 28 came from. But gap zero is not a draw from that distribution -- it is ONE NUMBER every ledger inherits, and for this chain it is 3. The family's true expectation is gapPairs - 1 + c(ZERO) = 30, and the measured 30.0120 sits 0.012 from it. The control settles it: a random-permutation chain has c(ZERO) = 0, its true expectation is 27, and it measures 27.1865. Half (b) held outright -- 0 of 2,000 ledgers admit a deletion-only forgery against a chance of 0.237, and the two conservation laws are visibly independent on that family: 173 of 126,000 subsets preserve the mixer head and 190 preserve the total, both at chance, and no subset does both. The registered failure route, a variance-to-mean ratio driven to zero by a permutation-like map, did not fire: 0.935. THE PRICE OF THE FAILURE IS THE FINDING -- c(ZERO) = 3 is F-A-UNIVERSAL-TWO-ENTRY-INSERTION-FORGERY, which is worth more than the prediction was. DISCLOSURE ADDED AFTER THE FACT, AND THE OUTCOME IS NOT CHANGED. The same re-audit that found AT1's maximum leg in the noise finds this one there too, in the other direction: re-run at twelve seeds the mean lands outside the registered band on FIVE and inside on SEVEN, so the recorded word FAILED was decided by the draw. The derivation says it had to be about half -- the true mean is the corrected chance of 30, the standard error is sqrt(28.06/2000) = 0.1185, and the registered line sits AT 30.0. AT3 STAYS FAILED for the same reason AT1 stays HELD. AND THIS IS THE BENIGN CASE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THE MALIGN ONE LEGIBLE: all twelve means lie within 0.271 of gapPairs - 1 + c(ZERO) = 30, so the criterion decided which word went in the outcome field and never touched the mechanism. A line in the noise corrupts a verdict; it does not automatically corrupt a finding, and telling those two apart is the whole of what a reader needs from this entry. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: THE FAILING LEG IS NOT DISCRIMINATING, which this note already said in its own words and the class tally never counted. AT3(a) lands outside its band on five of twelve seeds and inside on seven, so P(fail) is about a half and the recorded word was decided by the draw. THE FINDING SURVIVES DECISIVELY and this entry is the corpus's worked example of the distinction: the criterion decided the WORD and never touched the MECHANISM. c(ZERO) = 3 against a random-permutation control's c(ZERO) = 0, a corrected chance value of 30 against the control's 27 measured at 27.1865, and all twelve seed means inside 0.271 of 30 -- from which the two-entry universal forgery follows. A LINE IN THE NOISE CORRUPTS A VERDICT; IT DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY CORRUPT A FINDING. The outcome stands as recorded. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

entries.subject: What does the WIDTH of a ledger head buy a forger, and what does it not? A family of permutation-based heads at widths 1 through 6 trits -- 3 to 729 states, all exhaustively enumerable -- with AS's meet-in-the-middle join and second-preimage scan and AT's insertion and universal-pair attacks re-priced at every width, against exact finite-N nulls computed before the run
entries.claim: the ops currency is linear in the state count and width buys the forger's memory, not his time: over six widths with 24 random heads each, (a) the mean index of the first accepted compensating forgery divided by the exact finite-family null lies in [0.93, 1.07] at every width from 1 to 6 including width one where no carry exists, (b) the meet-in-the-middle join's yield ratio has a mean within 0.03 of 1.0 at widths 2 to 6 so AS's 6.99 operations per forgery is seven at every width while the table grows as 4N^2, and (c) the split-round head at widths 4 and 6 lies inside the random family's min-to-max range on both statistics
entries.note: Held on all three legs, and one of them is not evidence and is reported as such. (b) and (c) held with room: the join returns between 0.9933 and 1.0105 of ideal at every width from 2 to 6 and 1.0000 at width one where the left key map is a bijection, so AS's seven operations per forgery is seven operations per forgery at EVERY width and what width actually buys is the 4N^2 table -- 36 slots at width one against 2,125,764 at width six. All 20,199 rebuilt joined forgeries reproduce both heads. The split-round head sits inside the random family's range on both statistics at widths four and six, so the law is about width and not about D's mixer. (a) HELD AT WIDTH TWO BY 0.0002, at 0.9302 against a line at 0.93, and a redraw of the same population at four seeds gives 0.9684, 0.9243, 1.0275 and 0.9693 -- one of the four below the line. THE LEG IS NOT EVIDENCE. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: A SECOND LEG OF THIS PREDICTION IS NOT DISCRIMINATING AND NOBODY HAD LOOKED AT IT. A MIN-MAX CONTAINMENT OVER TWO DOZEN DRAWS IS A VERY WEAK CRITERION, and this one is exact rather than estimated. entries.claim: the collision law is the only square root in this thread and it has a floor: (a) the mean first-repeat index divided by the exact birthday null lies in [0.95, 1.06] at widths 4, 5 and 6 with no collision-free row at those widths, (b) the least-squares slope of log mean against log N over widths 2 to 6 lies in [0.45, 0.55] for the collision scan and in [0.95, 1.05] for the second-preimage scan, and (c) the shortfall at the narrow end is a multiplicity effect and not an ordering one -- at widths 1, 2 and 3 the measured mean divided by the mean over 200 random reshuffles of each row's own multiset of head values lies in [0.95, 1.05] at each of the three
entries.note: FAILED on leg (c) at width one alone, and the reason it fails is the mechanism it was asserting. At width one the measured scan finds no collision in any of 72 rows AND the reshuffled null finds none in any of 14,400 -- the row map is injective, so the multiset has no repeated value and no ordering can produce a collision. The ratio is 0/0. The registration named width one as degenerate in this very statistic's rationale and then included it in (c) anyway; that is the defect, and the sentence as written is not satisfied. (a) and (b) held. The first-repeat index tracks the exact finite-N birthday null to within 0.6% at widths four, five and six -- 1.0057, 1.0017 and 0.9938 -- with zero collision-free rows in 25,272 scanned, and the two slopes come out at 0.4642 and 1.0031 against registered bands at [0.45, 0.55] and [0.95, 1.05]. SO THE TWO ATTACK GOALS SEPARATE BY EXACTLY ONE SQUARE ROOT AND THE SEPARATION IS MEASURED. (c) held at widths two and three, 1.0208 and 1.0492, and the width-three value sits 0.0008 inside its line with a four-seed spread of 1.0492, 1.0034, 1.0320 and 0.9875, so that leg is thin too and is reported as such. The affine control settles the responsiveness: it is collision-free on every row at widths one and two and on one row in nine at widths three, five and six, where its mean first repeat at width six is 84.47 against a null of 34.51 -- 2.45x, so the statistic spans from undefined to well above its null before any subject value is read. ONE CORRECTION, FOUND AFTER THE RUN BY TWO READERS AND REPRODUCED HERE BEFORE BEING ACCEPTED. Leg (b)'s band [0.45, 0.55] was drawn around the ASYMPTOTIC exponent of the birthday law, and the asymptote is not what six points spanning 2.4 decades measure. The exact finite-N expectation is about sqrt(pi N / 2) + 2/3 and the additive term lifts the small-N points hardest, so THE IDEAL OBJECT'S OWN log-log slope over the registered window 2..6 is 0.4665, not 0.5. The measured 0.4642 therefore sits 0.0023 BELOW the ideal null rather than 7% below the wrong one -- agreement to half a percent, and a better result than the leg claimed. THE VERDICT DOES NOT MOVE: 0.4642 is inside [0.45, 0.55] and leg (b) HELD as registered, scored against the null that was registered. What moves is what the number MEANS. And the defect is real and is recorded separately: on three of the seven windows this sweep could have used -- 1..5, 1..4 and 2..4 -- the IDEAL OBJECT ITSELF scores under 0.45 and would have failed my own band. A reader gave the figure for widths 1..6, which is 0.4537; the registered window is 2..6 and it is 0.4665, so the correction is taken and the number is not. F-A-BAND-DRAWN-ROUND-AN-ASYMPTOTE-THE-WINDOW-CANNOT-REACH. CRITERION AUDIT, AFTER THE FACT: BOTH OF THIS PREDICTION'S REMAINING CRITERIA ARE NOT DISCRIMINATING, one on each side of the verdict. (c), the leg that FAILED, fails at width one where the statistic is 0/0 -- a degenerate criterion the registration had itself named as degenerate in this very statistic's rationale and included anyway -- and at width three it lands 0.0008 inside its line with a four-seed spread of 1.0492, 1.0034, 1.0320 and 0.9875. (b), which HELD, is the cousin defect already recorded as F-A-BAND-DRAWN-ROUND-AN-ASYMPTOTE-THE-WINDOW-CANNOT-REACH: the exact finite-N null's own slope over the registered window is 0.4665 and the ideal object misses the band on three of seven candidate windows. THE FINDING SURVIVES on (a), which is discriminating and held: the first-repeat index tracks the exact birthday null to within 0.6% at widths four to six (1.0057, 1.0017, 0.9938) with zero collision-free rows in 25,272, and the two fitted slopes separate the two attack goals by exactly one square root. The outcome stands as recorded. See F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE.

entries.claim: ADD equals TOPC with the 27-row addition table, exactly.
An interpreter bug that permutes the emulated semantics has an ORDER, and is invisible at layer counts divisible by it. Order 2 is masked at 2 layers; order 3 at 3.
Folding buys a level of emulation depth, not just instructions: the unfolded chain is refused at depth 4 and the folded one runs.
TGATE's three modes are not closed under composition: 6 of its 8 two-stage composites are not any TGATE mode. This is why TOP folds and TGATE cannot.
Reading -1/0/+1 as false/unknown/true, MIN, MAX and NEG are exactly the connectives of Kleene's strong three-valued logic. Excluded middle and non-contradiction both fail at unknown.
Base 3 is the cheapest integer radix by the radix-economy measure: representing a million values costs 40 in base 2, 39 in base 3, 40 in base 4.

Three-way dispatch beats two-way on the same machine by about half an instruction and a fifth of the code per decision point, and nothing at all when the decision is genuinely binary. Deep dispatch loses outright to an indexed jump: 149 cells against 30.

The top rung of the ladder is 531,441, numerically identical to the source conversation's figure, by coincidence. That figure counted two-stage configurations of 6-trit trytes (729^2); this counts elements of a monoid on 9 points (9^6). Both are 3^12 for unrelated reasons, and the conversation's claim about what it counted remains wrong.
The standard ternary inverter computes NEG on all three inputs; MIN and MAX are correct on all nine rows. Switch counts: STI 4, NTI 2, PTI 2, MIN 8, MAX 8.
The standard ternary inverter is not the only four-switch NEG in this model. Exhaustive search finds four distinct networks, and it is one of them.
The sum tree of a balanced-ternary full adder has only three distinct leaf selectors of nine, and the carry tree five, because both depend on a+b rather than on a and b separately.

An input gates a device and terminates a path, but never sources one: a conducting device between an input and a node transfers nothing, and the node is Z. Reachability starts at rails and only at rails.

The number of operand pairs on which the decoded adder settles in exactly thirteen passes is 251,505 â€” the same figure the monoid audits found for what positionwise logic plus one carrying ADD reaches at width two. Two different objects counted inside the same 3^12 space, landing on the same six-digit number.

The sum and carry halves of a balanced-ternary adder save in exactly complementary currencies, and for one reason. The low trit WRAPS, so its rows repeat across operand sums -- nine leaf selectors collapse to three -- but its cells never agree within a row, so it can never settle early. The carry STEPS, so its rows never repeat -- five of nine, no collapse -- but it is flat over stretches, so twelve of eighteen cells agree within a row and it settles early constantly.

The tmux/dmux split measured on one selector holds on a 27-way three-level read tree over stored cells: tmux reads all 27 addresses, dmux reads only the 9 whose every address trit is MID and never settles on the other 18.
Bus contention resolves to X only on the trits where the contending sources differ, so a double-enable fault is completely invisible when they hold equal values.

For a positionwise g, the map s -> s + g(s) is injective exactly when g is an orthomorphism, i.e. when t -> t + g(t) is itself a permutation of the trits. Exactly 3 of the 6 trit permutations qualify -- the identity and the two 3-CYCLES -- and all three involutions fail. Negation is the worst possible choice: s + (-s) = 0 collapses all 729 states to one.

Splitting the state and using one half to modify the other is invertible for ANY round function. With a NONLINEAR 27-entry round table, across 20 different tables, the cycle count runs 2..12 with mean 6.8 against ln(729)=6.6 and 19 of 20 inside two standard deviations -- consistent with a random permutation. The same structure with a LINEAR round function gives 92 cycles and order 8, so the structure is not what mixes: the round function's nonlinearity is.

Truncating any permutation to m trits gives perfectly uniform buckets by construction, so a truncated-collision count cannot distinguish a mixing function from a relabelling. A map proved to repeat every six calls scores 0.96x the random-function expectation, the same as every other permutation tested.

The split-state construction has EXACTLY ONE fixed point for every round table -- 1 in all 20 sampled, never 0 and never 2 -- where a random permutation gives Poisson(1) and would have none about 37% of the time. The state with L = R and round(R) = 0 is fixed; the round table is a permutation, so exactly one R maps to 0. That is a structural fingerprint rather than a statistic, and a fixed point is an input that no number of rounds ever moves. The standard remedy is a per-round CONSTANT, which collides with the one-function-called-repeatedly rule unless the round counter is carried inside the state.

The design intuition inverts between the two bases. In binary, linear operations are cheap and nonlinearity is something you construct by combining controls; in ternary, the simplest one-control conditional is ALREADY nonlinear and linearity is the special case you have to work to obtain -- t_b += t_a is affine and needs deliberate choosing, while "if t_a equals 1" is not and comes for free.

The group generated on 3^W accumulator states by every information-preserving instruction -- translation, negation, and all 216 reversible tritwise tables at every operand -- has order exactly 2^W * 3^((3^W - 1)/2). Nobody predicted a closed form; it was read off a ladder of exactly computed orders and then checked against every width the chain could reach.

An instruction has two different and equally correct erasure figures depending on where the state boundary is drawn. MIN reads as a single fixed 4.5033 bits when the operand is folded into the state, and as a range from 0 to 9.5098 when the operand is a known parameter -- and the fixed figure is exactly the mean of the range. Neither reading is wrong; the boundary is a modelling choice that must be declared before any number means anything.

All eight programs in this repository execute IN, and five of them cost exactly the same number of steps regardless of what they are given. Cost-invariance is the norm here rather than the exception, which nobody predicted and which is the single most important fact for any scheme that wants a step count to be evidence of work performed.

A hailstone rule of the form 3n + k cannot mix on a base-three machine. Multiplying by three always zeroes the low trit, so the low trit is k forever after the first climb: the value can never become divisible again and every trajectory runs to the fixed point of an affine map. Swept over all 729 inputs, 3n+1 terminates on exactly six of them -- the powers of three. Replacing the climb with 2n + low_trit mixes the residue and terminates on 363. Measured while choosing the rule, not predicted.

A ternary pitch space is simultaneously richer and poorer than the twelve-tone one, along two different axes, and neither prediction asked about the pairing. Z/27 has 61 trichord classes against Z/12's 12 -- five times the raw variety of three-note chords -- while having 4,755 times fewer transpositionally symmetric subsets by fraction. More things to say, far less structure to say them with.

Summed over the six just ratios swept, 27-EDO totals 45.48 cents of approximation error against 12-EDO's 64.41, and 81-EDO totals 22.84. A ternary division of the octave is a BETTER consonance approximator than the twelve-tone one, chiefly because 12-EDO's harmonic seventh is 31 cents out while 27-EDO's is 9. Nobody predicted this; AF1 only asked about individual intervals.

A program can have a wide live state and a nearly constant cost, or a narrow state and a wide cost range, and the two do not track each other. threeway has five live input words and a cost spread of 1.02x; countdown has one live word and a spread of 25.38x. So an implied receipt rests on THREE factors and not two: reachable state count, cost per evaluation, and the variance of the cost itself -- and if the third is near zero the other two do not matter, because a predictor guesses the commonest answer instead of tabulating.

A tabulator exploits TRAJECTORY CONVERGENCE, not a small state space, and the two come apart. The three-word program has a control space of 387 million against hailstone's 729 -- five hundred thousand times larger -- and still reuses each visited state 3.20 times against hailstone's 10.43. A subtractive inner loop converges onto shared suffixes whenever two inputs agree on the subtrahend, whatever their starting values. So an implied receipt rests on FOUR things and not three: state count, cost per evaluation, cost variance, and how tree-like the trajectory graph is.

A non-reversible feedback function does not merely merge some trajectories, it strands almost the whole state space. Tritwise MIN as shift-register feedback leaves 484,785 of 531,441 states -- 91.22% -- with no predecessor at all, and concentrates the survivors at a maximum in-degree of 729. AI4 predicted a quarter unreachable and a maximum in-degree of three; the real figures are far more extreme, which means a collapsing feedback is not a weak receipt but a state space that mostly does not exist.

The history operator gives a tabulator-proof trajectory graph, and self-reference is not why. Its step map is injective because it is built entirely out of addition, which erases nothing -- so a forgetful two-word carry has the property as fully as an append-only history. Self-reference in the strong sense is separately unavailable by the Ladder's own Coda III, which proves no system closes over its own semantics and shows that two of the three verdicts of nf(t) are not in the term. What was being asked for is reversibility, and it is cheaper than what was being proposed.

Where factor four is bought decides what it costs to keep. AI4 bought it by searching 19,683 tables for the 216 that work, and AJ1 by building a map deliberately out of addition -- both are properties of a particular program that a later edit could destroy. Choosing a reversible ALPHABET makes it a property of the language: 400 of 400 random programs have it, and no program can be written that does not. The same guarantee, at three different prices, and only the last one survives a programmer.
