Ternary modular addition -- the affine task, and the family the grokking literature studies almost exclusively -- generalises more slowly than a non-affine reversible sibling under a controlled comparison holding architecture, optimiser, split, seed and step budget fixed. Median 10,800 steps against 6,200, slower on 4 of 4 paired seeds, and on a fifth it failed to reach 90% inside 40,000 steps while the non-affine task succeeded on all five. Nobody predicted this; AM2 predicted the opposite.

A Davies-Meyer feed-forward whose message enters the data path through the SAME group operation as the nonce is not a puzzle at all. h(m,n) = P(m + n) - n collapses identically to g(m + n) + m with g(u) = P(u) - u, verified on all 531,441 pairs, so every message is one puzzle shifted. One 729-entry inverted index of g then solves every mineable message in 1.54 lookups against a brute force of 3.0 to 305.2, and correctly declares the rest unmineable rather than failing on them. Keying the permutation with the message instead -- true Davies-Meyer -- destroys the identity and returns the hit-count variance to within 3% of binomial at every difficulty. A fix that removes the symptom is what confirms the cause.

The stranded messages and the shortcut are one object, not two findings. g(u) = P(u) - u has an image of 465 of 729 digests, and 729 - 465 = 264 is EXACTLY the number of messages AN3 counted as unmineable at maximum difficulty. A message is mineable at the tightest target precisely when its shifted target lies in that image, so the size of the image is the mining participation rate. Nothing predicted the two numbers would be the same number.

An affine puzzle gives every message exactly the right NUMBER of solutions and puts them in the wrong PLACES. At k = 3 every message has exactly 27 valid nonces, as a bijection must, yet a sequential scan needs 248 attempts to reach one where the null says 27 -- so the honest miner does nine times the expected work while the algebraic attack does one operation. The gap between honest and attacker is therefore wider than AN2 measured, and a hit COUNT alone would have missed it.

A machine built from AK's language cannot destroy a secret, so it cannot run a trusted-setup ceremony. Injectivity is closed under composition (AK2), so no program maps two distinct starting states to the same final state: two different secrets stay distinguishable for ever, and every intermediate state determines the initial one. Erasure, as this project defines it, is exactly the collapse that cannot occur — so the ceremony's "and then delete s" step is not merely unperformed but INEXPRESSIBLE in the language. The property AK was built to guarantee is the property that forbids it.
entries.argument: Corollary of AK2 and the definition of erasure. E = 0 for every program in a language all of whose primitives are bijections, and a secret is destroyed only when the final state is constant in it — which requires E > 0.

entries.claim: A Lamport key costs b preimages per position and log_b N positions, so b / ln b per value -- minimised at b = e, which puts three ahead of two by 5.4% asymptotically. That advantage does NOT hold at every width, because the position count is an integer: sweeping ten digest sizes, binary wins at 256 and 1024, the two tie at 64 and 4096, and ternary takes the other six. An asymptotic argument does not settle a particular width.
entries.argument: Cost per value is b * log_b N / log N = b / ln b, whose derivative vanishes at b = e; 3/ln3 = 2.731 against 2/ln2 = 2.885. The per-size flip follows from ceil(log_b N) being a step function: at N = 2^k the binary position count is exact while the ternary one rounds up.

entries.claim: A summed ledger head and a hashed one carry the same 9.5098 bits about a history of any length, so a collision COUNT cannot separate them. What separates them is findability. Over one six-entry ledger, all 21,840 compensating pairs -- add d to one entry, subtract it from another, leave the total alone -- were accepted by the summed head, every single one, and 26 were accepted by the split-round mixer fed forward, against a chance rate of 29.96. The control says the compensating structure is doing the work: of the 4,368 single edits, which move the total, the summed head accepted 0 and the mixer accepted 7 against a chance rate of 6.
entries.argument: The summed head is linear in the entries, so a compensating pair is not a search at all -- it is one equation with a solution by construction. The mixer chain a' = P(a + e) - e has no such solution, so a forger is reduced to trying, and 26 of 21,840 is what trying gets.

entries.claim: The N^(L-1) collision count is a property of an IDEAL hash, and the concrete mixer is not one. Over all 531,441 two-entry ledgers the summed head is exactly flat at 729 preimages per head, while the split-round chain ranges from 629 to 851 -- 17 percent above the ideal at its peak. No head is unreachable, so the chain is onto and the bias is in the spread rather than in the range.
entries.argument: The summed head is flat because addition is a bijection in the last entry, which fixes the preimage count at N^(L-1) by construction. The chain step P(a + e) - e is NOT a bijection in e -- that non-invertibility is exactly what AN registered it for -- so its preimage counts are free to vary, and they do.

entries.claim: Once verifying dominates bandwidth, an authenticated tree wants the branching factor its leaf count is written in. Of 18 leaf counts of the form 3^k, 15 take branching factor three; of 19 of the form 2^k, 13 take four. The two shapes are almost equally represented in the sweep, which is the entire reason AQ1 saw a 21-21 tie rather than a result. NARROWED BY SET AR, AND THE ORIGINAL WORDING IS KEPT ABOVE BECAUSE IT IS WHAT WAS FOUND: this holds only under the constraint that every level of the tree uses the SAME arity, which is the one constraint every tree in AQ's sweep was built under. Lift it and 25 of these 45 leaf counts change shape, 11 of the 18 powers of three among them -- N = 729 prefers the radix sequence [4,4,4,4,3] to six threes. It prefers it by 0.0178% of the total cost, so the surface this preference was read off is flat to four decimal places. A TREE BRANCHES IN ITS OWN BASE IS A PROPERTY OF CONSTANT TREES.
entries.argument: At large gamma the cost is dominated by depth times arity, and depth is ceil(log_b N). When N is an exact power of b the ceiling is tight and no level is wasted; when it is not, the top level is partly empty and paid for in full. A leaf count of 3^k therefore pays nothing for branching by three and rounds up for branching by four, and the reverse holds for 2^k.

entries.claim: Set AQ's registered control could not have detected the failure it was written to detect. Its two cost terms are the same pseudorandom draw, so its total is d*NOISE[b]*(1+gamma) and gamma factors out entirely: its optimum is invariant in the exchange rate at every one of the 45 leaf counts. A post-hoc control drawing the two terms independently gives 7 distinct optima with 131 backward steps and a narrowest optimum of 207, against the vector regime's 61 optima, 0 backward steps and narrowest optimum of 3 -- which is what actually establishes that the vector regime is structure rather than the shape of the arithmetic.
entries.argument: A control exists to show that the instrument does not manufacture the effect. If the swept parameter cancels out of the control algebraically, the control is constant in exactly the dimension the claim is about, and it can only ever agree.

entries.claim: In this cost model a radix sequence's total depends on it only through its MULTISET of arities -- indeed only through the depth d and the sum of the arities. A tree that is three at the top and nine below costs exactly what nine at the top and three below costs. There is no schedule to choose, only a multiset.
entries.argument: Every regime charges a per-level weight and the weights add, so the total is sum over levels of w(b_i), which is symmetric in the levels. For the merkle and vector regimes w is affine in b, so the sum collapses further to a function of d and sum(b_i) alone. This is what makes the whole search reduce to MINSUM(d, N) and it is immediate from the construction rather than discovered.

entries.claim: In the merkle regime, letting the arity vary buys exactly nothing at any leaf count and any exchange rate. The all-twos tree is optimal, and it is optimal by proof rather than by sweep.
entries.argument: Merkle cost is (H + gamma) * sum(b_i - 1). For every integer b >= 2, b - 1 >= log2(b) with equality only at b = 2, so sum(b_i - 1) >= log2(prod b_i) >= log2(N). The cost is an integer multiple of (H + gamma), and the all-twos tree attains ceil(log2 N), which is the least integer above that floor. No sequence can do better and only all-twos attains it.

entries.claim: The cost surface over arity choices is nearly flat where AQ read a preference off it. Admitting radix sequences changes the SHAPE of the optimal tree at 25 of AQ's 45 leaf counts -- including 11 of the 18 powers of three, AQ's own headline case, where N = 729 wants [4,4,4,4,3] rather than six threes -- while changing the COST by 0.0133% to 0.0251% at the median, and 13 of the 25 shape changes are worth under 0.5%.
entries.argument: At those leaf counts the sequence achieves the SAME gamma-charged quantity d + sum(b_i) as AQ's constant tree and simply spends fewer levels reaching it, so the entire saving is per-level byte overhead. At N = 3^12 both cost 48 units of verify and the sequence uses ten levels where the constant tree uses twelve.

entries.claim: A leaf count is helped by letting the arity vary EXACTLY when its own optimal tree is not a constant one. Over the 7,169 leaf counts of the deep window there are no exceptions: 1,025 are unhelped and the same 1,025 have a constant optimum. The unhelped counts are the powers of FOUR rather than powers in general, because four is the arity the optimum wants; 2187 = 3^7 is helped.
entries.argument: One direction is immediate -- if the optimal sequence is constant it is available to the constant optimiser, so nothing is gained. The other direction is not forced by anything in the construction and is what the measurement adds: no leaf count has a strictly non-constant optimum that merely ties the best constant tree.

entries.claim: Registering a prediction does not make it a prediction. A read-only audit of all 181 predictions registered as of 1acfeee scored 25 of them DECORATIVE -- the answer and its derivation both standing in the registration's own text, over quantities the registrant stipulated -- and 7 it could not call. PUBLISHED: 181 registered, 149 held, 32 failed, a 17.7% failure rate. CORRECTED to what was genuinely at risk: 149 registered, 117 held, 32 failed, 21.5%. Both numbers are true and they answer different questions, so both are kept and neither replaces the other; 181 predictions were registered and that is a fact about what happened. The failures were never the problem -- all 32 are real, and not one of them is among the 25, which is the rule validating itself, since a fact that was never at risk cannot fail. What is not evidence is 25 of the 149 successes.
entries.argument: The rule scored only what the registration itself wrote down, and it read that text with `git show <registered_at>:<tool>` rather than from the working tree, so no later editing of a docstring can move a verdict. Four routes to decorative: arithmetic performed inside the block; forcing by a theorem the block states; restatement of a definition or of a sibling's conclusion; and a commitment about the phase's own paperwork rather than about the machine. The 25 are spread across 18 of the 43 sets and the rate does not fall over time, so this is a habit rather than an early-project artefact. IT IS NOT THE SAME AXIS AS `basis`, which looks as though it should have caught it: only 5 of the 10 `proven` predictions are decorative, and 20 of the 25 decorative ones are marked `measured`. A derivation can be genuinely at risk because the derivation may be WRONG -- AK1's registration typed a group order at 25 digits where the true value has 28, and held only because the claim named the group rather than the numeral. AQ was the only one of the 43 sets audited that wrote `AT RISK` lines into its registration and the only one that scored zero decorative; AR, the 44th, was registered the same way. That is a sample of two, and two agents happening to have been told about it is not an antibody, which is why the annotation is now compulsory rather than advisory. Finally the count is a FLOOR: the rule cannot see arithmetic a registrant did silently, and six of the 25 -- Q4, R5, G1, AJ4, AE2, AL2 -- are contestable. Conceding all six leaves 19 and does not change the verdict.

entries.claim: The mixer's ledger head is a commutative sum in disguise. With g(u) = P(u) - u the step a' = P(a + e) - e is a + g(a + e), and substituting u_k = a_{k-1} + e_k -- a triangular and therefore invertible change of variable -- gives head = g(u_1) + ... + g(u_L). And because P is a permutation, every step is a bijection in the accumulator, so a forgery touching positions i and j has head' = head EXACTLY when the accumulator after max(i, j) is restored: 218,400 of 218,400 agreements over twenty drawn ledgers' full compensating families, with 274 accepts among them so the agreement is not vacuous.
entries.argument: Both are algebra, not measurement, which is why they are here rather than among the predictions -- and both are checked exhaustively anyway, because T-TRANSCRIBED-TABLE was a comment that was right and a transcription that was not. The consequences are what matter. The chain linearises into a sum over a reparametrisation of the entries, which is the ledger-direction residual of AN2's collapse: the entry does not commute out the way the message did, but the head is still additive in u. And the merge-point equivalence means a forger never evaluates the tail and can walk the chain BACKWARDS from a target head, which is the whole basis of the meet-in-the-middle attack that prices the mixer at 6.99 ops per forgery.

entries.claim: The published compensating sweep enumerates every forgery twice. forge(E, i, j, d) and forge(E, j, i, -d) are the same forged ledger, so ledger-audit's 21,840 ordered tries are 10,920 DISTINCT forgeries and its 26 accepts are 13. Ratios are unaffected, because the chance rate of 29.96 is double-counted the same way; F-FINDABILITY-NOT-COUNT is correct as stated.
entries.argument: It matters for one thing and matters a lot for it: DISPERSION. A Poisson process scored over a doubled count shows a variance-to-mean ratio of 2, so any claim about how the accept count varies across ledgers is off by a factor of two unless it is written over distinct forgeries. AS1 is written that way. It also changes how the headline reads -- 13 against a chance of 14.979 is half a standard deviation low, where 26 against 29.96 invites the reading that the mixer is doing something. It is not.

entries.claim: For an adjacent position pair, an accepted compensating forgery IS the realisation of a two-round differential of g, and a delta whose differential cell is empty cannot be accepted at all: 0 accepts in 2,669,929 tries, which is 36.67% of the family. The accept rate then rises linearly with the cell -- 0.98, 1.97, 3.07, 3.74, 5.65, 5.40 and 6.65 times chance at cells one through seven.
entries.argument: Write A for the change the first edited entry makes to the accumulator and t for the tritwise input difference it induces at the second; the merge-point equivalence says the forgery is accepted exactly when g realises t -> -A at that ledger's own u. So the number of u realising it -- the differential cell -- is the accept probability times 729, and an empty cell is a certainty rather than a small probability. This is the only place in set AS where the residual algebra gives a forger something with certainty, and it is what AS4's halving is made of.

entries.claim: Priced rather than counted, the mixer's advantage over the summed head is about a factor of seven, not the factor of 840 a per-try collision rate suggests. A meet-in-the-middle join over four modified entries enumerates 532,485 forgeries of one ledger -- same arithmetic total, same mixer head -- at 6.99 ops per forgery and 2,125,764 table slots, against a measured brute-force baseline of 4,414 ops per accepted forgery over the same family: a 632x cut. The summed head needs no search at all, about one op.
entries.argument: The 840 comes from a family with ONE free parameter, where a single constraint costs a single tryte of search whatever the accumulator is. Give the forger four entries and the constraints are two -- the arithmetic total and the head -- against four unknowns, and the chain's one-tryte state lets both halves be tabulated and joined. The enabling property is not the mixer's algebra but its width: nine and a half bits of accumulator, so the state space squared fits in two million slots. THE ATTACK IS GENERIC AND THAT IS THE POINT. Nothing in it uses the split round; it would work against any iterated head of this width, which is why the ledger question is a width question rather than a mixing question.

entries.claim: D's split-round permutation has exactly ONE fixed point, so there is exactly one u with g(u) = 0, and therefore -- from every one of the 729 accumulators -- exactly one entry value that leaves the mixer head unchanged. Verified at all 729. The same object read the other way: g's image is 465 of 729, so 264 accumulator increments are unreachable in a single step.
entries.argument: By D1 the step from accumulator a with entry e is a + g(a + e), so the entry e = u - a with g(u) = 0 does nothing at all. THIS IS THE ATTACK SURFACE SET AS DID NOT TOUCH. Every forgery in the set keeps the ledger at six entries, so none of them can use a free move that only an INSERTION makes available. A forger who may lengthen the ledger gets a mixer no-op at every position of every ledger; the entry's VALUE is forced, so the arithmetic total moves and the insertion has to be paid for elsewhere, but that is a cost rather than an obstacle and nothing here measures it. Recorded because an unexamined attack surface reported as silence is exactly how 26 against 29.96 stood unexamined since the ledger was built.

entries.claim: There are exactly THREE pairs of entry values -- (136, -136), (295, -295) and (362, -362) -- each of which, prepended to ANY ledger of ANY length, leaves both the arithmetic total and D's split-round mixer head unchanged. The forgery costs TWO added entries and ZERO operations, needs no knowledge of the ledger's contents at all, and is precomputable once for the mixer rather than per ledger. Verified by rebuilding both heads on 420 drawn ledgers across seven lengths including the empty one.
entries.argument: The accumulator before the first entry is the tritwise identity on EVERY ledger, so gap zero is one fixed accumulator that every ledger stands on. Inserting x then y at one gap returns the accumulator to where it was exactly when a is a fixed point of T_x : a -> STEP[STEP[a][x]][-x], which by AS's D3 is a composition of two bijections in the accumulator and therefore a permutation for every x; the arithmetic total is restored because y is the arithmetic negation of x by construction. Over all 729 accumulators the number of x fixing each sums to 741, a mean of 1.0165, and 256 accumulators admit none -- so a pair need not have existed at all, and on a control chain built from a random permutation the identity accumulator admits ZERO. It admits three here. THIS IS THE ANSWER TO WHAT AN INSERTION COSTS, and it is cheaper in both currencies than anything in set AS: AS's meet-in-the-middle join pays 6.99 operations per forgery and 2,125,764 table slots, its brute-force baseline 4,414 operations, and this pays nothing and grows the ledger by two. It is also what made AT3 fail: the registered chance value of 28 treated all 28 gap pairs as random accumulators when one of them never is, and the family's true expectation is gapPairs - 1 + c(ZERO) = 30 against a measured 30.0120.

entries.claim: Priced in the two currencies stated before the run, every insertion attack in set AT costs less SEARCH than either of set AS's edit attacks and pays instead in ledger GROWTH. The universal pair: 0 operations, +2 entries, no knowledge of the ledger. The universal prepend run: 0 operations, +243 entries, no knowledge of the ledger. The shortest no-op run: about 5,100 operations for a certainty rather than a chance, +4.93 entries on average and +1 on 0.90% of ledgers. Two free insertions: about 2,380 operations per accepted forgery, +2 entries. Against AS's cited figures for a forger who may not lengthen the ledger: 4,414 operations per forgery by brute force, or 6.99 amortised over a 2,125,764-slot meet-in-the-middle join.
entries.argument: The two currencies are not convertible and no exchange rate is invented, so the comparison is stated as a pair rather than a ratio. What the pair says is that the mixer's factor of seven over a summed head, which AS established for a forger who may only edit, DOES NOT SURVIVE THE ENLARGED CLASS: against a forger who may insert, the mixer's search cost falls to zero and the entire remaining defence is whether anyone counts the entries. That is a statement about the VERIFIER rather than about the accumulator, and it is the same shape as AS's own conclusion that the ledger question is a width question rather than a mixing question -- one level further out.

entries.claim: The fixed point of D's split-round permutation is at value -336, so the forced no-op entry at gap zero -- the one every ledger shares -- is -336, its generator in Z_729 is 393, and its order is 243. A run of exactly 243 prepends of that one value therefore forges any ledger of any length, verified by rebuilding on 240 drawn ledgers across six lengths.
entries.argument: The EXISTENCE of a universal prepend run is derivable from AS's F-EVERY-ACCUMULATOR-HAS-A-NO-OP-ENTRY plus the fact that a_0 is the tritwise identity, and is in AT's NOT REGISTERED block as I4. Its LENGTH was not: 486 of the 729 possible values have order 729, 162 have 243, and three have order at most 3. Which one it is decided AT1's low-side failure route, since an order of 1 or 3 would have bounded every ledger's minimum at three and driven the mean under 4.0. It is 243, so the route did not fire. Recorded because the value of u* was nowhere in this repository before this set -- AS printed only that P has one fixed point.

entries.claim: The surface set AT leaves open, measured rather than named. A forger who pays for one insertion with one compensating EDIT has no free parameter left -- the inserted value is forced by the gap and the edit is forced by the arithmetic total -- so the family is 42 candidates on a six-entry ledger. Over 500 drawn ledgers, 28 of 20,970 candidates are accepted, 0.973 times chance, on 24 of the 500 ledgers.
entries.argument: An unexamined attack surface reported as silence is how 26 against 29.96 stood unexamined since the ledger was built, and how the insertion question itself waited for set AT. So this one is measured. What is NAMED AND NOT MEASURED, in the same spirit: three or more free-value insertions, which is a 729^(k-1)-parameter family that an AS3-style meet-in-the-middle would price and that this set does not build; insertion against a structured rather than uniform entry distribution; and any family that edits more than one entry alongside an insertion. The k >= 3 route is the one worth taking next, because AT3's two-insertion family already yields 30 forgeries per ledger from 20,412 candidates and a third insertion multiplies the parameter space by 729 while adding one constraint.

entries.claim: A ledger forger handed a ledger pays the STATE COUNT and a forger who may choose both ledgers pays its SQUARE ROOT, and the two laws are measured across six widths rather than assumed. Over widths 1 to 6 with 24 random heads each, the first accepted compensating forgery arrives at index 3.0, 8.4, 27.9, 82.1, 241.5 and 702.6 against exact nulls of 3, 9, 27, 81, 243 and 729, fitting a slope of 1.0031 against log N; the first colliding pair of equal-total length-two ledgers arrives at 4.39, 7.52, 12.03, 20.24 and 34.30 against exact finite-N birthday expectations of 4.4583, 7.1981, 11.9577, 20.2105 and 34.5100, fitting a slope of 0.4642. So the birthday law is the wrong law for a ledger and it is wrong by a factor of two in the EXPONENT -- read as a design rule it demands twice the width a second-preimage forger actually costs.
entries.argument: The ledger publishes two heads and a forgery must reproduce both, but one of them can always be solved rather than searched: a compensating pair preserves the arithmetic total by construction, so the mixer head is the only constraint and hitting it is a 1-in-N event, giving a geometric first hit at N. A collision is a birthday problem in the same N because the forger fixes the total once and varies within it. The separation is therefore not a property of the mixer at all -- it is a property of which question is being asked, and a design that reads the birthday number off a table and calls it the required width has priced the wrong attack. Both figures are ops in AS's unit, so they are comparable to AS's 4,414 and 6.99 without conversion.

entries.claim: AS's meet-in-the-middle join returns between 0.9933 and 1.0105 of its ideal yield at every width from 2 to 9 states through 729, and exactly 1.0000 at width one, so its amortised cost is 6.94 to 7.17 operations per forgery AT EVERY WIDTH. The 6.99 AS measured at 729 states is not a fact about 729 states. What grows with width is the table: 4N^2 slots, 36 at width one against 2,125,764 at width six, a factor of 59,049 across five trits while the cost per forgery does not move.
entries.argument: The join enumerates N^2 rows on each side into an N^2 keyspace at 7N^2 operations, so seven operations per forgery is arithmetic once the YIELD is ideal, and the yield being ideal at every width is the measurement. AS3 registered the failure route -- two half-tables whose key sets coincide return the sum of squared counts, 2.0 times ideal -- and it did not fire at any width. So the honest statement of what width buys against this attack is a memory requirement rather than a work factor, and a forger who can hold the state space squared pays the same seven operations however wide the head is.

entries.claim: AT's universal pair -- two prepended entries, zero operations, no knowledge of the ledger -- is not a property of 729 states. Over 400 random heads at each of six widths, the fraction of heads admitting at least one is 1.0000, 0.5275, 0.6075, 0.6625, 0.6000 and 0.6450, and width six is not the rarest. Unconditioned by fixed-point count the same fractions are 0.7025, 0.6450, 0.6425, 0.6100, 0.6625 and 0.6550. About two heads in three admit a zero-cost forgery at every width in the sweep, and widening the head 243-fold does not reduce that.
entries.argument: The zero-op forgery lives at ONE distinguished accumulator -- the tritwise identity, which every ledger stands on before its first entry -- and the number of entry values fixing it is a draw whose mean is one whatever the state count is, because a -> STEP[STEP[a][x]][-x] is a permutation for every x. A quantity whose mean does not depend on N cannot be driven down by raising N. This is the sharpest thing the set has to say about the design question: in the operations currency width is worth its own state count, and against this family it is worth nothing at all.

entries.claim: Three of this set's twelve registered legs landed within 0.005 of their band and all three HELD: AU1(a) at width two at 0.9302 against a line at 0.93, AU2(c) at width three at 1.0492 against 1.05, and AU3(c) at 0.0545 against 0.05. Redrawn, the first straddles its line -- 0.9684, 0.9243, 1.0275, 0.9693 over four seeds -- and so does the third, 0.0494, 0.0441 and 0.0597 over three. The four earlier bites of T-CRITERION-IN-THE-NOISE were all found because a criterion FAILED. A criterion in the noise that passes is the same defect with nothing to make anybody look.
entries.argument: The class's own remedy is to widen the line until it cannot flip or to report the quantity without a bound, and neither remedy is triggered by a passing check -- the suite goes green, the manifest records HELD, and the reader has no signal at all. The only thing that surfaced these three was measuring the seed-to-seed spread of every leg that landed close to its band, whether it passed or failed, which is now what the tool does. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING: a failing criterion audits itself and a passing one does not, so the corpus's four recorded bites are a lower bound on how often the defect has occurred and say nothing about how often it has been benign.

entries.claim: At width one, every one of 4,800 second-preimage scans over 24 heads and 200 drawn six-entry ledgers returns the SAME index: 3, without exception. There is no distribution. At three states the compensating family's first accepted forgery is always the third candidate in the scan order, so the measured mean of 3.000 against an exact null of 3.000 is an exact agreement that is not a statistical one.
entries.argument: Width one is the point where arithmetic and tritwise addition are the same operation -- 0 of 9 pairs differ, against 380,178 of 531,441 at width six -- so the two-group mismatch every attack in this thread runs against is absent by construction. The narrow end of a width sweep is where a distributional statistic stops being distributional, and reporting the mean alone would have shown a perfect fit and hidden that there was nothing to fit. This is why the whole histogram is printed rather than the mean.

entries.claim: Set AT registered twelve legs across four predictions and TWO of them were criteria sitting in the noise. AT2's maximum leg failed and is recorded as a bite of T-CRITERION-IN-THE-NOISE. AT1's maximum leg has the same defect -- a bound on a maximum whose line sits one step above where the uniform null's own 2,000-draw maximum lands, crossed by the subject at two of twelve seeds -- and it landed INSIDE its band, so it was recorded as a clean HELD and counted toward the held column. The two sit THIRTY-THREE LINES APART IN ONE REGISTRATION -- AT1 at line 154 and AT2 at line 187 of the registration as db57466 holds it, same author, same day, same error. One is in the corpus and one was invisible until set AU supplied the rule that found it.
entries.argument: The corpus's count for this class is therefore not the number of times it happened; it is the number of times it happened AND produced a visible failure, because the noticing was done by the outcome rather than by anyone looking. Every criterion equally in the noise that landed inside its band was written down as HELD. That makes the recorded bite count a lower bound whose gap nobody can size from the record, and it points at the HELD column as the place to look rather than the failed one -- which inverts this project's own habit, since METHOD.md's argument rests on the failures being where the value is. AND THE REMEDY HAS THE SAME FLOOR ONE LEVEL UP. The first version of this disclosure put the null's exceedance probability at 3.9%, estimated from 50,000 draws containing exactly ONE exceedance; drawn at 500,000 it is 7.7% with a 95% interval of [0.044, 0.109] over 20 exceedances. A tail read off a single observation, written into the disclosure about reading tails badly, is the third instance of this shape in one thread and the cheapest to have avoided. The antibody is that tailNull now returns a confidence interval with every estimate, so an exceedance rate resting on a handful of draws announces itself rather than being quoted as a point.

entries.claim: A registered band can be placed around a limit the measurement's range cannot reach, and then it is scoring the window rather than the subject. AU2(b) put the collision slope in [0.45, 0.55] around the birthday law's asymptotic 0.5. Fitted over the registered window of widths 2 to 6, the EXACT finite-N birthday expectation's own log-log slope is 0.4665; over widths 1 to 6 it is 0.4537; over 1..5, 1..4 and 2..4 it is 0.4439, 0.4315 and 0.4490, all three BELOW the band's own lower edge. So on three of the seven windows this sweep could have chosen, a perfectly ideal head would have failed the registered band. The measured 0.4642 sits 0.0023 below the ideal null on the window actually registered, not 7% below the asymptote.
entries.argument: The exact expectation is about sqrt(pi N / 2) + 2/3, and an additive constant lifts the small-N points hardest, so a log-log fit over a narrow window is biased downward and approaches the asymptotic exponent only as the window widens: 0.4665 at 2..6, 0.4770 at 2..8, 0.4877 at 2..12, 0.4950 at 2..20. Six points spanning 2.4 decades cannot see the asymptote and no widening this machine can afford would fix it -- 2..12 already needs 531,441 states. THE GENERAL SHAPE IS T-CRITERION-IN-THE-NOISE'S COUSIN AND IT IS NOT THE SAME DEFECT: a criterion in the noise is one the RUN can move, and this is one the run cannot move at all because the ideal object misses it too. The remedy is the one this repository already applies to null models -- compute the null at the width you are measuring rather than in the limit -- and it has to be applied to the CRITERION and not only to the comparison value.

entries.claim: Widening a construction can turn it into the IDENTITY at one width while leaving it healthy at the widths either side, and no statistic of its OUTPUT DISTRIBUTION can say so, because the identity is a permutation and every permutation has the same output distribution -- which is `D4`, where truncating any permutation was found uniform by construction and the obvious test disqualified. D's split round widened to w/2-trit halves is a permutation at widths 2, 4 and 6 and has exactly one fixed point at 4 and 6 -- and at width TWO it has NINE fixed points on nine states, which is to say it is the identity map. Eight rounds of a one-trit Feistel over a three-entry S-box return every state to itself. Checked at every even width rather than at the endpoints, which is the only reason it was found. THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS CLAIM SAID NO DISTRIBUTIONAL STATISTIC COULD SEE IT AND THAT WAS FALSE. A reviewer falsified it in eight lines and the measurement is now part of this finding rather than a footnote to it: the maximum cell of the differential table of g = P - I is 9 of 9 at width two, the absolute ceiling, against 8 of 81 at width four and 8 of 729 at width six. When P is the identity g is identically zero, so every input difference maps to the zero output difference with probability one. A DIFFERENTIAL TABLE DOES NOT MERELY SEE THE COLLAPSE, IT READS ITS MAXIMUM -- which is the same signature AS2's affine control was built to show the statistic can reach, at 729 of 729.
entries.argument: THE DEFECT IS INVISIBLE TO TWO OBVIOUS CHECKS AND LOUD TO A THIRD, AND GETTING THAT WRONG COST THIS FINDING A SENTENCE. Asking which input positions can influence which outputs -- a dependency-closure computation -- says nothing about whether the influences CANCEL, so a family can have complete closure at every width and still be a relabelling at one of them. Every distributional figure computed on that width would then be measuring the identity and reporting it as a mixer. The endpoints are exactly where this hides: widths 4 and 6 both behave, and a family checked only at the width it was ported from and the width it is aimed at would have passed. The general rule is that a structural invariant of a widened construction must be asserted at EVERY width in the family, and asserted as a separate thing from reachability. WHAT IS BLIND AND WHAT IS NOT, stated precisely because the first version of this finding got it wrong. Blind: any statistic of the OUTPUT DISTRIBUTION, by D4 -- all permutations share one, so bucket counts, collision counts and preimage profiles are identical for the identity and for a good mixer. Blind: dependency closure, which computes may-influence and cannot represent cancellation. NOT blind: the differential table, which reads its ceiling. So the honest rule is not that the collapse is invisible but that it is invisible to exactly the checks a width sweep is most likely to run, and the one that catches it is the one AS2 already built.

entries.claim: The corpus-wide sweep F-THE-BITE-COUNT-IS-WHAT-FAILED-NOT-WHAT-HAPPENED named as the thing that would size the gap, and recorded as not run. IT HAS NOW BEEN RUN. Of the 165 predictions scored AT RISK, 50 place a MAGNITUDE LINE; 32 of those admit a null that can be drawn without inventing the chance model. THIRTY-ONE OF THE 32 WERE SCORED, and they carry 55 LEGS, 43 held and 12 failed. The 32nd is AQ4, which arrived in this class after the sweep had run and HAS NO SCORED LEG: a line-bearing prediction whose null is drawable and which nobody has drawn. It is a gap, not a result, and it must not be counted into the 55. THE UNIT IS THE LEG AND NOT THE PREDICTION, because a prediction with three legs can hold on the two that were evidence and fail on the one that was not. SIXTEEN OF THE 55 LEGS ARE NOT DISCRIMINATING -- the null crosses the registered line between 5% and 95% of the time -- 9 of them held and 7 failed. Four more CANNOT GO THE OTHER WAY, at P(recorded verdict | null) >= 0.99, and one is undetermined at the draw count run. So 12 of the 43 held legs and 8 of the 12 failed legs are not evidence about the subject. THE SIXTEEN, WITH THE LINE, THE NULL AND THE CROSSING RATE. H1(a) FAILED, spread within 3x, null host load, 3.72 on one run and 2.89 on the next. H2(a) HELD, a 50,000-device solve under one second, null host load, a duration line of the class bite two outlawed, margin 14.18x against a measured 14.35x swing. D4 FAILED, truncated collisions separate a mixer from a positionwise map, null any permutation, P = 1. AM2 FAILED, the affine task groks soonest, null one paired comparison, P = 50%. AO1(a) FAILED, E within 5% of 0.8265, null a random ceremony map, 64 of the tool's own 400 draws cross, 16%. AO4 HELD, exposed secrets within 10% of both 268.4 and 264, null a random map on 729 points over 8,000 draws, P(the null misses either band) = 6.54% CI [6.02, 7.10], measured 252 sitting 1.27 sd inside. AR1 HELD, the varying optimum costs at least 85% of the constant one at every cell, null 300 matched redraws over [2, 8192] x 8 decades, P(cross) = 9.0% CI [6.3, 12.8]. AR2 HELD, the largest single-leaf jump less than half as large, null 500 matched redraws, P(cross) = 87.5% CI [71.9, 95.0] on the 32 non-degenerate draws -- and the recorded HELD is the null's MINORITY outcome, so that leg still carries about three bits. AT1(b) HELD, no ledger needs more than 12 insertions, null uniform, P(cross) = 7.7% CI [4.4, 10.9], 2 of 12 seeds. AT2(d) FAILED, no ledger needs more than 100, null uniform, about 58%. AT3(a) FAILED, mean within 2.0 of 28.0, 5 of 12 seeds fail and 7 hold. AU1(a) HELD, ops ratio in [0.93, 1.07], measured 0.9302, four further seeds straddle. AU1(c) HELD, the split head inside the random family's min-to-max range, null EXACT by exchangeability -- a 25th draw falls outside the min-max of 24 with probability 2/25 = 8% per statistic. AU2(b) HELD, collision slope in [0.45, 0.55], the ideal object misses on 3 of 7 candidate windows. AU2(c) FAILED, reshuffle ratio in [0.95, 1.05] at widths one to three, failed at width one where the statistic is 0/0, and 0.0008 inside its line at width three. AU3(c) HELD, slope gap at least 0.05, measured 0.0545, 3 of 12 seeds cross. THE FOUR THAT CANNOT GO THE OTHER WAY are AP2(a), AP2(b) and AP2(c), all HELD at P = 1 by exact algebra and two explicit witnesses, and AR4, FAILED at 500 of 500. THE ONE UNDETERMINED is AR3, whose crossing rate is 4.2% CI [2.8, 6.3] -- an interval straddling the bar, so the classification is undecided rather than the measurement.
entries.argument: THE TWO SEVENS ARE DIFFERENT SETS AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE LIST. The seven failed NON-DISCRIMINATING LEGS are H1(a), D4, AM2, AO1(a), AT2(d), AT3(a) and AU2(c). The seven recorded FAILURES that rest ENTIRELY on a criterion that was not evidence are AO1, AT2, AT3, AU2, AM2, D4 and AR4. Same cardinality, membership differing by exactly one element on each side: H1 also failed on leg (b), which is discriminating at some five standard deviations, so H1's FAILED is carried by a leg the null could not have produced; AR4 is not a noise line at all but a line the null clears with probability one, and its single leg is the whole of its verdict. THE CORRECTION IS ASYMMETRIC IN A WAY THAT MAKES IT WORSE. The failed column is close to a census, because those legs were found BECAUSE they failed and somebody went looking; the held column is one auditor's sweep. The held figure is therefore a floor and the failed figure is nearly complete, and the true imbalance runs further toward the held side than the recorded split suggests. And one artefact has to be stated beside the failed rate or it reads as an indictment: noise lines are over-represented among failures BY CONSTRUCTION, since a non-discriminating line fires on the null between 5% and 95% of the time and a discriminating one almost never does, so conditioning on failure concentrates them. That is partly selection -- and it is also the direct quantification of how many recorded failures may be draws rather than refutations. A LINE IN THE NOISE CORRUPTS A VERDICT AND DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY CORRUPT A FINDING. In all seven of the affected failures the verdict is non-evidence and the finding survives, on evidence disclosed in each entry rather than asserted here: AT3(a) produced c(ZERO) = 3, AT2(d) produced the draw-the-null's-tail rule out of the null's own draws, AO1(a) produced the distributional-null rule, D4 produced AN1 -- and D4 is the case where the non-discrimination IS the finding, because a criterion no permutation can fail is exactly what disqualifies the obvious test. AM2 is the sharpest illustration of the split: its criterion is a coin on one paired comparison, and the run's own five seeds put the non-affine task faster in 4 of 4, which is stronger than the criterion ever asked for. NOTHING HERE IS RE-SCORED. Every outcome and every at_risk value stands exactly as its results commit left it, because that ordering is the only property of this record a later edit cannot fake; `reaudits` is untouched. What is recorded is what a criterion was WORTH, never what a verdict should have been.

entries.claim: A TOOL THAT READS REGISTRATION TEXT OUT OF HISTORY CAN BE BROKEN BY HISTORY IN A WAY NO CHECK AT HEAD CAN SEE. The criterion-discrimination sweep located each set's registered predictions by recovering `git show <registered_at>:<tool>` and searching it for the header `PREDICTED OUTCOMES`. Set AQ's tool used `REGISTERED PREDICTIONS` at the time it was registered. The extractor emitted a no-block line, the screener printed a NOCHUNK marker, and the classification silently fell back to the manifest's one-line summary -- so AQ IS THE ONE SET IN THE CORPUS WHOSE REGISTERED CRITERIA WERE NEVER READ AT ANY POINT IN THE AUDIT, and it is the set whose classification was then disputed and found wrong on all three of its predictions. AND THE DEFECT IS INVISIBLE FROM THE CURRENT TREE. At HEAD `tools/branching-audit.js` carries `PREDICTED OUTCOMES`; the header was normalised at some later commit. Checked at each set's OWN registered_at, exactly one of the 47 lacks the header the extractor was looking for, and it is AQ. A grep over the working tree says all 47 are fine and always were.
entries.argument: This is the same shape as a filter that quietly matches nothing -- the sibling defect in this thread compared a classifier's return value against a constant it can never equal, reduced its population to empty, and printed four rows of plausible p-values from no data -- but with a worse property: the evidence of the fault has been edited out of the place anyone would look. A staleness check, a lint, a grep, a test over `tools/` at HEAD: none of them can see this, because the tree is correct now and the fault is in what the tree USED to say. AND THIS WAS NOT A GAP NOBODY NOTICED, WHICH IS THE WEAKER AND LESS TRUE STORY. `test/test-findings.js` documents the mechanism at HEAD, in the comment beside the at_risk validator: it says outright that the check reads "the tool AS IT STANDS", that the registered block is what `git show <registered_at>:<tool>` returns, that a line edited in later "is visible in that history rather than invisible to it, but it is not this check that would notice", and that the completeness check in section 2 has the same defect -- with moving both to the registration commit called "one coherent change and not a patch for this one". So someone checked, wrote down exactly this, named the second affected check, judged it benign and deferred. WHAT MADE THE JUDGEMENT WRONG WAS NOT THE REASONING BUT A ROUTINE CLEANUP: a later commit normalised the header, and the evidence that would have shown the deferral coming due left the working tree. A deferred defect whose evidence is subsequently tidied away stops being deferred and starts being invisible, and nothing in the deferral could have anticipated that. Section 2's completeness check still has the same defect and is still unguarded: a named remaining silence rather than an oversight. The general rule is that ANY GUARD OVER REGISTRATION TEXT MUST RUN OVER EACH SET'S OWN registered_at RATHER THAN OVER THE WORKING TREE, which is the same reason the decoration audit scored against `git show` in the first place: a tool's current wording is text that may have been edited since. It generalises past this audit to every tool that does `git show <commit>:<path>` -- the recovery step needs an assertion that it recovered something, and the vocabulary it recognises has to be the union over history and not the spelling that happens to be current.

entries.claim: Comparing two functions at a single input and concluding they are equal. Bit the mixed-TGATE test, the folded-vs-unfolded programs, and the TOP-vs-ADD comparison, where 81 of 19,683 tables matched at one pair.

A hardcoded count in a test or a document going stale when the thing it counted grew. The closure test kept passing against an opcode list the source no longer had; test-findings.js miscounted its own prediction sets; and the README stated both a check total and a prediction tally that had drifted. The first two were fixed by deriving them. The third could not be owned by any one suite, because it is the sum of all of them, so run-all.js sums the suites and test-findings.js recomputes the tally. Fifth bite: the decode audit hardcoded the direct-encodable width as 6 in its cost section, two lines below the search that had just measured it as 5 -- so it printed a saving the measurement immediately above it had already refuted. The cost section now reads the search result. A constant is not safe merely because the thing it duplicates is nearby. Fifth bite, in a REGISTRATION rather than in prose about a result. AK1 typed A_27 = 27!/2 as a 25-digit number when it is 28 -- three zeros dropped, a factor of a thousand -- inside the commit that registered the prediction, where it could not be corrected afterwards without breaking the protocol. It cost nothing only because the tool COMPUTES the factorial and compares against that, rather than against the digits in the docstring, so the run verified the claim and the typed number was never load-bearing. AGENTS.md already says to derive constants and never hardcode them. The rule was obeyed in the code and broken in the sentence next to it, which is where it is easiest to break and hardest to notice.
Writing through a missing label produced an undefined address, so the write silently did nothing. The core interpreter ran with no control register and no complaint.
.fold reading nine cells from a table that was shorter, silently borrowing whatever followed it.

Confusing ran out of budget with finished. A search that exhausts its depth limit, one that hits its size cap, and one that genuinely closes are three different outcomes; conflating them produced a false negative verdict on V3. It recurred in the E sweep, where one counter held both settled-sooner-than-predicted and needed-longer-than-predicted, and the correctness check was skipped for the second bucket -- so an exhaustive claim was published while resting on an unmeasured decomposition. That time the numbers happened to be right: the second bucket was empty. Report the outcomes separately and check that they sum to the total. Third bite, this time in a CHECKER rather than an instrument: the staged solver was compared against solve() by crediting agreement only when both settled, so the cases where both agreed precisely that the network does NOT settle were counted as disagreements, and the tool declared its own results suspect.

Switch-level reachability traversing THROUGH a driven node. A path from one rail that touches another rail and continues out of it makes correct circuits look contended. Rails and inputs are ideal sources and must terminate a path.

The measuring tool, not the thing measured, producing the failure. V3 read depth exhaustion as saturation; W2 traversed reachability through rails; X5 keyed a network by ordered terminals when D4 says terminals have no order; G4 dropped a qualifier that was present in its own registration and counted a quantity restated in a second set as colliding with itself. Each reported a verdict about the world that was a fact about the instrument. When a result contradicts a prediction, suspect the instrument first, and check the loop against the sentence that was registered. Fourth bite: the terminal audit held its storage cells with hold=LOW, which is the WRITE configuration -- the hold switches are n-types at threshold HIGH, so LOW opens the feedback loop and every cell floats. Every one of 81 cases in both families read Z, and the audit would have reported the roadmap blocking question as answered NO. A verdict of "nothing works" against a family that demonstrably works is the instrument. Fifth bite: the memory rig built its decoder with the first address trit MOST significant and its read tree with that trit LEAST significant. Each half was internally consistent; together they addressed different words for 18 of 27 addresses, so writes appeared to land in the wrong place and every read-back failed. Two halves of one address path disagreeing about endianness reads exactly like a broken circuit. Sixth bite: the interconnect rig named its sources `src0_0`, `src1_0`, ... and SEEDED them, without building anything behind them. A seed is an initial value, not a driver -- T5 says reachability starts at rails and only at rails -- so every source resolved to Z on pass one and stayed there. Both topologies routed Z, which read as "interconnect does not work at all" rather than "these are not sources". The same fact this repository already records as "an input gates but never sources", arriving in a form nobody recognised. Seventh bite, and inverted: a TEST CASE accused a correct instrument. The Schreier-Sims verification paired a 3-cycle with a 25-cycle and called the pair "A_27"; between them they move 25 of 27 points, so the tool returned 25!/2 -- exactly right for what was actually built -- and was scored WRONG. When a verification case fails, the case is as suspect as the thing it checks. Eighth bite: the sequencer rig called tAdderCell without its TAG, which names every internal node of the cells two tables. All three cells received the tag `undefined`, so their internal trees shared node names and merged into one circuit -- the incrementer resolved to unknown and the sequencer appeared to visit two states instead of twenty-seven. An omitted parameter that looks optional silently welded three circuits together. Ninth bite, in the same phase and pointing the other way: the handshake section counted the two driving values that DISABLE the loop as "settled cleanly", which would have reported a self-timed handshake as working on the strength of two circuits in which no handshake occurs. A false positive and a false negative from one tool in one run. Two more, found by reconciling this list against results/07-negative.md, which had one occurrence the manifest never named and lacked two the manifest did: the detector truth table hand-copied from a comment and INVERTED, which produced 36 failures out of 54 -- every one where the middle word disagreed with the selected word and none where they agreed, the exact signature real contention would leave, reading as the publishable headline that the decoded selector cannot read storage. Two views of one list drifted apart in opposite directions, which is what a second copy of a record is for and against. Twelfth bite: AB2s first erasure census folded the operand INTO the state, which is a defensible boundary and not the one AB2 asked about, so MIN read as a single fixed 4.5033 bits when the registered prediction was about a range from 0 to 9.5098 -- a correct computation about a different question, which would have recorded a prediction as FAILED when it held in full. Thirteenth bite, and it produced the most interesting wrong headline yet. AC1 detected whether a program reads input with a regex anchored at the start of the line, which misses every LABELLED instruction -- threeway.tasm carries "body:   IN". So the audit reported a program that never reads input whose step count nonetheless varied with the input: a deterministic machine charging different amounts for data it never touches, which would have been the finding of the set. It was a broken parser standing next to an exported real one. Replaced with the assembler's own tokenizer, which moved the count of input-reading programs from five to eight and changed what AC1 was even about. Fourteenth bite, and it pointed the flattering way, which is the dangerous one. AD2's tabulator memoised only TERMINATING values, so each of the 366 divergent inputs walked its full three-thousand-step guard, learned nothing, and left the next divergent input to do it again: 1,098,362 evaluations to price 729 inputs. It reported a patient predictor as three hundred times WORSE than simply re-running, which is exactly the answer that would have made AD2 fail and the implied receipt look sound. Non-termination is an answer too, and a correct tabulator records it; walking until the path meets either a known value or itself resolves every state once and costs 728. An instrument that errs toward the hypothesis under test will not be caught by finding the result surprising, because it is not surprising. Fifteenth bite, and the SAME MECHANISM AS THE ELEVENTH in the same thread. AH2's reuse instrument walked every hailstone input to a 3,000-step guard, including the 366 that never terminate -- and those cycle through a handful of states three thousand times each, so hailstone measured 1,513x reuse against its true 10.43x. AD2's first tabulator failed for exactly this reason a few sets earlier and the repair was recorded there. A guard counted as work is apparently not a lesson that transfers by having been written down once; it has to be looked for. The repaired figure of 3,777 visits reproduces AD2's number exactly, which is the cross-check that says the two sets now measure one thing. Sixteenth bite, and a new flavour: MISREADING SOMEONE ELSE'S SPEC. AI1 implemented the Ladder's history operator with "SUM prev" read as the sum of everything so far INCLUDING the most recent term. That generates 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 -- the powers of two -- and agrees with Fibonacci at exactly one of forty terms, so the audit reported that an external artifact's central operator does not do what it says. The Ladder's own derivation line states the indexing unambiguously, L(n+1) = 1 + SUM L(0..n-1), so prev EXCLUDES the last term. One term short and the sequence changes species. Every earlier bite in this list was a wrong instrument pointed at this project's own subject; this one was a wrong instrument pointed at somebody else's finished work, where the failure mode is publishing a refutation of a thing you misread. Seventeenth bite, in AN: the shift attack wrapped a value that was already a value in val() a second time, shifting every nonce it produced by TRYTE_MIN. It reported solving 0 of 729 messages at the two hardest difficulties and looked entirely plausible on its own -- a structured puzzle that resists a structural attack is a perfectly sensible-sounding result. What caught it was the CONTRADICTION with AN3, which had measured 465 of those same messages as mineable by exhaustive search. The antibody is not a code review but a cross-check: the fast attack and the slow sweep must agree on WHICH messages are solvable, not merely produce numbers of a believable size.

A prediction failing on an assumption it never stated rather than on the quantity it asked about. X2 asked which seeds are self-consistent and assumed every seed resolves; two do not. The assumption, not the answer, was the falsifiable part.

A sampling instrument that was not sampling. A seeded generator multiplied a 31-bit seed by a 31-bit constant, which overflows the 53 bits a JS number holds exactly, so the low-order bits it returned were rounding noise: three of its eight node names were drawn essentially never and no random network ever floated or contended. It looked like 400 trials and was closer to 400 repetitions of one. Random input needs a vacuity check on what it actually produced, not on how many times it ran.

A consistency check that treated a legitimate intermediate state as a defect. It demanded that tools/ and the manifest prediction sets be equal in number; they are equal only between phases, because registering a tool predictions and recording its results are deliberately separate commits. During a registration there is one more tool than there are sets, and that is the protocol working. The check now names the pending tool instead of failing on it. Second bite: the design-folder status-marker check scanned for bare vocabulary words with a word boundary, and a new trap id -- T-COMPUTED-CONTROL-UNKNOWN-AT-PASS-ONE -- contains UNKNOWN between hyphens. The check failed a document whose vocabulary was entirely correct, because an identifier is not a marker.

An instrument that searched for a value it could have verified. Finding the exact pass count by scanning k = 1 upward cost up to eighty solves per input on a 1,776-switch network and did not finish inside ten minutes. The count is the same for every input, so it needs finding once and checking twice thereafter -- settles at k, does not settle at k-1. Two solves, not eighty.

A measured result stated as a property of the SUBJECT when it was a property of the DESIGN measured. Z2 swept buffer placements in one family of trees and concluded a depth floor for ternary at any price; a different selector beat it. E4, and Y2 and Z5 before it, measured raw-select circuits and concluded settling time is never data-dependent; a decoded selector made it data-dependent. Both times the numbers were right and the noun was too big. Before writing ternary, or this model, ask whether the sweep visited more than one design. Third bite, and the first scored against this project's own prose rather than against a sweep. AE2 and AE4 measured exactly one musical affordance -- the availability of transpositionally symmetric chords -- and the write-up headed the section "and here ternary is genuinely worse", generalising from one affordance to an entire art form. Consonance, rhythm, contour and timbre were untouched, and so was the distinction between ternary as a TUNING and ternary as an ADDRESSING scheme, which is the layer a 3x3 pad grid actually uses. The tell is the same every time: the sweep visited one thing and the sentence named a category. Ask what the sweep did NOT visit before choosing the noun. Sixth bite, in AU4, and this time the control caught it rather than a reader. The set's random-head family is CONDITIONED on having exactly one fixed point, because an entry is a no-op at an accumulator exactly when their tritwise sum is a fixed point of the head, so a head with none has no insertion family at all -- the conditioning is what makes the family comparable to D's P. AU4 registered a band on the fraction of heads admitting a zero-operation universal pair and it failed at width two, at 0.5275 against [0.56, 0.70]. The UNCONDITIONED family at the same width reads 0.6450, comfortably inside. So the failure is a property of the design decision and not of width, and it was visible only because both families were run. At nine states one constraint is a ninth of the object; the same conditioning is invisible at 729.

A measurement over a corpus that the measurement is then written into. G4 surveyed the manifest for repeated integers, and recording its own result added those integers to the manifest a second time -- as the values it had excluded -- so the next run found them colliding and the prediction failed against its own record. Nothing was wrong with the world or the first answer. If a result is stored where it will later be read as data, exclude the storing record from the read, and derive the exclusion from something structural rather than an id.

A registered criterion whose verdict depends on run-to-run variation. H1 predicted a spread under 3x and measured 3.72 on one run and 2.89 on the next, either side of its own line, so the same world produced both a pass and a fail. The attempt to salvage a more robust shape from it flipped too. A threshold placed near the noise floor is a defect in the prediction rather than a fact about the subject; either widen it until it cannot flip, or measure the quantity and report it without asserting a bound. Second bite, and it was sitting inside the suite that records the first. test-headroom section 5 checked "the six-trit adder is sweepable inside an hour" against a LIVE timing. It passed on an idle machine and failed at 1.84 h inside a full suite run on a loaded one -- the same world returning both verdicts. Section 4 of the same file already refuses to assert durations and enforces that refusal by grepping itself; section 5 was quietly doing what section 4 forbids, four sections below the comment explaining why not to. The repair is the one the class prescribes: assert the RATIO, which survives any host -- a 50,000-device sweep costs about 80x a 624-device one -- and report the hour figures without checking them. On the loaded host the measured sweep budget is 335 devices against H2 recorded 4,806, so the figure was never a constant of nature and is now labelled as a measurement taken on a stated machine. Third bite, in AO1: a 5% band was registered around a null that 400 draws confirm exactly, but scored against ONE fixed pseudorandom map -- which turned out to sit 2.09 sigma out, while 336 of 400 draws would have passed. The criterion did not depend on run-to-run variation this time; it depended on WHICH SAMPLE WAS FROZEN AS THE CONTROL, which is the same defect seen from the other side. A single fixed pseudorandom object is one draw and a null model is a distribution; comparing them directly scores the seed rather than the claim. The remedy is to register the band against the control own empirical spread, or to sweep. Fourth bite, in AT2, and it is the form that does not need run-to-run variation at all: a bound on a MAXIMUM placed by arithmetic about a MEAN. The exponential counting heuristic that predicted the mean minimum insertion count to within 0.03 at length six put the chance of a length-two ledger needing more than 100 insertions at essentially zero; drawn directly, the uniform null exceeds 100 in 22, 25 and 33 of 50,000 draws at three seeds, so 2,000 draws expect about one and the registered line had roughly a 58% chance of firing on the null alone. The measured 146 is not evidence that the subject's tail is heavier than chance -- the null's own maximum is 243 at every seed. The remedy is the class's own: before registering a bound, DRAW THE NULL'S TAIL rather than integrating an approximation that was fitted to its centre. Fifth bite, in AU, and it is the form nothing makes you look at: THE LINE PASSED. Three of set AU's twelve registered legs landed within 0.005 of their band and all three held -- AU1(a) at width two at 0.9302 against a line at 0.93, AU2(c) at width three at 1.0492 against 1.05, and AU3(c) at a slope gap of 0.0545 against 0.05. Redrawn at further seeds the first straddles its line (0.9684, 0.9243, 1.0275, 0.9693) and so does the third (0.0494, 0.0441, 0.0597). The four earlier bites were every one of them found because a criterion FAILED; a criterion in the noise that passes leaves a green check, a HELD in the manifest and no signal at all. So the remedy has to run on passes too: measure the seed-to-seed spread of every leg that lands near its band, whatever its verdict, and say on the record that the leg is not evidence. F-A-LINE-IN-THE-NOISE-THAT-PASSES-IS-THE-SAME-DEFECT. Sixth bite, in AT1, and it is the first one this catalogue counts that DID NOT FAIL -- which is only on the record because AU's fifth bite supplied the rule that finds them. AT1 registered that no ledger of 2,000 needs more than 12 insertions and measured 10; the leg HELD and was written down as clean. Drawn directly, the uniform null's own maximum over 2,000 draws is MOST LIKELY 10 as well, and P(a null maximum exceeds 12) is 0.077 over 500,000 draws, so the line sat one step above where chance lands unaided and the measured value is the null's modal outcome. Re-run at twelve seeds the subject's maximum spans [9, 13] and crosses the registered line at two of them. THE LEG WAS NEVER MEASURING THE SUBJECT. And the shape is what makes it worth a number rather than a footnote: AT2's maximum leg has the identical defect, is THE VERY NEXT PREDICTION in the same registration block, same author and same day (AT1 opens at line 149 of the registered tool and AT2 at line 183; the phrasing is structural rather than a line count because a line count does not survive a reformat, and the count this catalogue first carried was wrong in both direction and magnitude) -- and AT2 FAILED, so it became bite four while AT1 became nothing. The counting is done by the outcome and not by anyone looking, which is why the tally for this class is a floor of unknown height rather than a census. Two remedies, and they are different. For a criterion the DRAW decides, draw the null and report the leg as not evidence whatever its verdict. For a criterion placed around a LIMIT -- AU2(b)'s band drawn round the birthday law's asymptotic exponent, where the exact null's own slope over the registered window is 0.4665 and the IDEAL OBJECT fails the band on three of seven candidate windows -- no draw helps, because nothing can satisfy it. F-A-LINE-IN-THE-NOISE-THAT-PASSES-IS-THE-SAME-DEFECT, F-THE-BITE-COUNT-IS-WHAT-FAILED-NOT-WHAT-HAPPENED and F-A-BAND-DRAWN-ROUND-AN-ASYMPTOTE-THE-WINDOW-CANNOT-REACH are three faces of one error: A LINE PLACED BY REASONING ABOUT A LIMIT RATHER THAN ABOUT THE THING BEING MEASURED. Compute the criterion at the width, the length and the seed you are actually measuring. AND ONE CONSEQUENCE OF COUNTING A RETROACTIVE FIND, WHICH THE FLOOR CAVEAT DOES NOT COVER. The tally could previously rise for one reason only -- a class recurring -- so its TREND was readable as a defect rate. It can now also rise from re-audit EFFORT, and a jump from 6 to 9 could mean three fresh mistakes or one reader sweeping three old sets. AND THE TREND IS NOW UNREADABLE AS A RATE: the level is a floor of unknown height, and the slope is a mixture of recurrence and attention with no way to separate them from the number alone. That matters because METHOD.md publishes the summed bite count as prose, where a rise reads as the project getting worse at something. Counting the retroactive find is still right -- the tally was always a lower bound on occurrences and a retroactive find moves it toward the truth rather than away, and refusing it would preserve a precise answer to a narrow question over an imprecise answer to the real one -- but what it is a count OF changed when the first one was admitted. BITES SEVEN TO FOURTEEN ARRIVE TOGETHER, FROM ONE SWEEP BY ONE READER, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS SHOWN RATHER THAN THE NUMBER BUMPED. A corpus-wide sweep scored 55 legs that carry a magnitude line and a drawable null, and found 16 of them not discriminating. Seven of those 16 are legs this catalogue ALREADY counts: H1(a) is bite one, AO1(a) bite three, AT2(d) bite four, AU1(a) with AU2(c) and AU3(c) bite five, and AT1(b) bite six. One more, AU2(b), meets the sweep's criterion and is NOT counted here, because it already has a home in the cousin class as F-A-BAND-DRAWN-ROUND-AN-ASYMPTOTE-THE-WINDOW-CANNOT-REACH and counting it twice would inflate exactly the number this audit concludes is unreadable. That leaves EIGHT new instances -- D4, AM2, AO4, AR1, AR2, AU1(c), H2(a) and AT3(a) -- and 6 + 8 = 14. THE UNIT IS THE LEG, STATED BECAUSE THE EARLIER ENTRIES WERE NOT MADE UNDER THAT CONVENTION: bite five bundles three of set AU's legs as one, while AT1(b) and AT2(d) are two separate bites from a single registration block written the same day by the same author. Those two conventions cannot both be right, and choosing between them moves the published total by more than the number of new instances being added. SEVERAL OF THE EIGHT HAD ALREADY BEEN DESCRIBED IN THEIR OWN SETS' PROSE AND COUNTED NOWHERE, AND THE EXACT NUMBER IS NOT ESTABLISHED. AT3(a) is the undisputed and the sharpest: its own note says the recorded word was decided by the draw, in the entry the defect corrupted, and the tally never moved. D4 says its test is disqualified in its own note; AO4's tool printed that it held only because its band was twice AO1's; AR1's note records a null tail above the subject's worst cell. THE SPLIT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED AS A COUNT: no membership rule for "disclosed" was fixed in advance, two careful readers derive it differently, and a third scan reached neither because it read the prediction entries while some of the disclosure lives in set-level and results/ prose. A precise-looking number that two readers derive differently is worse than no number, and this class's subject is unearned numerals. THE CLAIM DOES NOT NEED THE COUNT: for the tally to be a floor it is enough that some instances were written down and none of them moved a number, and that much is not in dispute. Disclosure and counting are separate acts, and only counting moves a number anybody reads. AND THE COUNT SHOULD NOW BE READ AS A CENSUS OF ATTENTION RATHER THAN AS A RUNNING TOTAL. This entry already warned that the tally can rise from re-audit EFFORT and that its slope mixes recurrence with attention; a jump of eight at once, from one sweep, makes that warning load-bearing rather than cautionary. Nothing about the project got worse between bite six and bite fourteen. Somebody looked. Note also what is NOT counted here: the four legs the sweep found could not go the other way at all -- AP2(a), AP2(b), AP2(c) and AR4 -- are not lines in the noise, because no draw is involved and the criterion had one reachable value. They are recorded as their own category in F-A-LINE-THE-NULL-CLEARS-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE rather than inflating this class.

A fact that could have been RUN was hand-copied instead. The terminal audit seeded a detector output from its truth table as written in a comment. The comment was right; the transcription inverted it, putting an n-type gate above its threshold so a selector leg conducted on exactly the addresses where it must be off. The result was not noise: 36 of 54 cases failed, every one of them a case where the middle word disagreed with the selected word and none where they agreed -- the exact mechanistic signature real contention would produce, and a plausible headline finding. A wrong instrument does not look wrong. When a value is derivable by running a two-line network, run it rather than copying it.

A control signal that is a COMPUTED node rather than a primary input is unknown on the first pass of the fixed point, and unknown conduction is treated as possible -- so on pass one it bridges or breaks everything it gates. Counted ONCE, not twice: B1a predicted exactly this shape for a decoded selector's middle leg in its own registration commit BEFORE the run, which is the protocol working rather than a trap anyone fell into. It bit in C, where nothing in the registration anticipated it: every hold gate in a 27-word array is a decoder output, and all 26 unaddressed words went to X on every write. The cells hold perfectly when hold is a primary input and not at all when it is a decoder output. The fix is not a workaround -- solve the control cone on its own and seed it. The general shape is that a circuit correct at its fixed point can be unreachable from a cold start, and the larger the control fan-out the more it takes with it.

A correct computation scored a prediction wrongly because the measurement drew its state boundary somewhere the prediction did not. N1 asked whether a BUILD puts MID on a node when the registered rule was whether the FUNCTION requires it, and scored the detector FORCED while the next section built the same function with zero taps. AB2's first census folded the operand into the state, which is a defensible boundary and not the one AB2 asked about, so MIN came out as a single fixed figure while the clauses spoke of a range, and AB2 would have been recorded as FAILED. Both readings are defensible and the registration did not say which it meant, so the honest diagnosis is an ambiguous registration as much as a mis-scoped instrument. The defence is to state the boundary in the registration and to report every reading the question admits rather than one. Third bite, and this one arrived from a LATER set rather than from the instrument itself. G4 censuses the manifest for integers appearing in both the vocabulary half and the circuit half; its classifier returns a third value, other, for a tool requiring neither, and the crossing test counted other as a side. Set AB then recorded 19,683 -- the size of the two-input tritwise function space, which Q also holds -- and a set belonging to NEITHER half read as crossing between them. The computation was correct and the question was not the registered one. Scoped to the two named halves, which is a structural exclusion rather than an id. Fourth bite, and the registration had stated the boundary CORRECTLY. AG1's docstring said a tabulator indexes what varies between runs of the same program, and that a program's own instructions are identical every run and cost it nothing -- then the code poisoned every cell of the assembled image and counted whatever moved the price. That measures the program rather than the input, so interp-core came out at 73 live words and all nine programs cleared AD4's threshold: a result that would have reported an implied receipt as already working here. Naming a class does not stop you walking into it. Once the definition is written down the only place the gap can hide is between the docstring and the code, so that is where to look.

A tool that is exercised only through require(), so the path it takes when actually RUN is never covered. The erasure audit was made silent on import by a mechanical rename of every console.log call to log -- which rewrote the body of log itself into a call to itself. The tool crashed with a stack overflow on every single run, and every check in its suite stayed green, because a test that imports the module sets MAIN false and no print path ever executes. Nothing about the numbers was wrong; the program was simply broken in the half nobody looked at. The antibody is a check that spawns the tool as a subprocess and asserts it exits cleanly and printed every section, made affordable by an environment variable that caps its most expensive sweep. Mutation-tested: reintroducing the recursive definition turns all three of those checks red.

A control that cannot fail, because the parameter the claim is about cancels out of it. Set AQ's control gave its two cost terms the same pseudorandom draw, so the exchange rate factored out and its optimum was constant in exactly the dimension the sweep was measuring -- it could only ever agree, whatever the trees did. The antibody is to check the control's RESPONSIVENESS before reading its verdict: the suite now asserts that the registered control is invariant in gamma at all 45 leaf counts, so the defect is recorded as a fact rather than left looking like evidence, and a second control with independent draws carries the discriminating work.

entries.subject: A summary statistic has hidden the failure three times
entries.claim: A summary statistic has hidden the failure three times
entries.note: D4 failed because truncating any permutation gives perfectly uniform buckets, so a collision count cannot tell a hash from a relabelling. AN1 failed because the hit-count MEAN looked healthy while one 729-entry index solved every mineable block in 1.54 lookups. AO1's erasure read 0.89 bits while 252 of 729 secrets were recovered exactly. Three sets, three different quantities, one shape: the statistic that summarises is not the statistic that binds. Security is a minimum and every one of these was a mean.

entries.subject: Four jobs want the same property and three of them want it backwards
entries.claim: Four jobs want the same property and three of them want it backwards
entries.note: The receipt needed in-degree exactly one, so nothing merges and a tabulator has nothing to amortise. The puzzle needs in-degree ABOVE one, or AN2 inverts it at one lookup per solve. The ceremony needs collapse, and cannot have it on a reversible substrate at all. The ledger wants in-degree one again, because an entry that merges is an entry lost. Same measured property, four requirements, and they do not agree. Whenever this project has found a primitive that suits one of them, that suitability has been the disqualification for the next.

entries.subject: A hash's energy floor and its security are the same property
entries.claim: A hash's energy floor and its security are the same property
entries.note: AN2 showed an invertible candidate dies to a 729-entry table at one lookup per solve, so a hash MUST erase. Landauer charges kT ln 2 per bit erased. SHA-256's compression takes 768 bits and emits 256, so it destroys at least 512, which is 2.94e-18 J per double-SHA attempt at 300 K. You cannot make a hash cheaper than its erasure without making it invertible, and an invertible hash is not one. The catch is the distance: a modern ASIC sits about 5.1e6 above that floor, so physics is real and is nowhere near binding. Six point seven orders of magnitude of headroom is a market, not a wall.

entries.subject: The wall is program-relative versus function-relative
entries.claim: The wall is program-relative versus function-relative
entries.note: Ladderlang's latency_floor proves that no machine of any width runs a given term in fewer than its depth cycles, axiom-free.
